sentences.zh: 李密李密，字玄邃，本遼東襄平人。

translations.literal: Li Mi, styled Xuansui, was originally a native of Xiangping in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi, whose courtesy name was Xuansui, came originally from Xiangping in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 魏司徒弼曾孫，後周賜弼姓徒何氏。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Bi, Minister of Education of Wei; the Later Zhou bestowed on Bi the surname Tuhe.
translations.idiomatic: A great-grandson of Bi, who had served as Wei’s Minister of Education, his family received the surname Tuhe from the Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 祖曜，周太保、魏國公；

translations.literal: His grandfather Yao was Grand Tutor and Duke of Wei in Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yao had been Grand Tutor and Duke of Wei under the Zhou;

sentences.zh: 父寬，隋上柱國、蒲山公，皆知名當代。

translations.literal: his father Kuan was a Sui Superior Pillar of State and Duke of Pushan—both were renowned in their time.
translations.idiomatic: his father Kuan was a Sui Superior Pillar of State and Duke of Pushan, and both men were famous figures of their age.

sentences.zh: 徙為京兆長安人。

translations.literal: The family was later registered as natives of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The clan was later reclassified as residents of Chang'an in the metropolitan region of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 密以父廕為左親侍，嘗在仗下，煬帝顧見之，退謂許公宇文述曰：「向者左仗下黑色小兒為誰？

translations.literal: Mi held office as a Left Attendant of the Inner Guard through his father's privilege; he once stood below the imperial weapons, and Emperor Yang glanced at him. Withdrawing, the emperor said to the Duke of Xu, Yuwen Shu: "Who was that dark little boy below the left guard just now?
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's yin privilege Mi became a Left Attendant in the inner guard. Once while he was stationed beneath the imperial arms, Emperor Yang noticed him and, when he had withdrawn, asked the Duke of Xu, Yuwen Shu, "Who was that small dark-complexioned boy on the left just now?

sentences.zh: 」許公對曰：「故蒲山公李寬子密也。

translations.literal: " The Duke of Xu replied: "He is Mi, son of the late Duke of Pushan, Li Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: " The Duke of Xu answered, "That was Mi, son of the late Duke of Pushan, Li Kuan.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「個小兒視瞻異常，勿令宿衛。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "That boy's glance is unusual; do not assign him to palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The way that child looks about is out of the ordinary. Do not keep him on night watch in the palace.

sentences.zh: 」他日，述謂密曰：「弟聰令如此，當以才學取官，三衛叢脞，非養賢之所。

translations.literal: " Another day Shu said to Mi: "Young brother, you are so clever—you should seek office through learning and talent; the Three Guards are a tangle of petty posts, no place to nurture the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: " On another occasion Shu told him, "With gifts like yours you ought to win office through scholarship, not clerking in the Three Guards—that clutter of petty posts is no nursery for true talent.

sentences.zh: 」密大喜，因謝病，專以讀書為事，時人希見其面。

translations.literal: " Mi was greatly pleased and accordingly pleaded illness, devoting himself solely to reading; people of the time rarely saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: " Delighted, Mi thereupon claimed illness and devoted himself wholly to study, so that contemporaries seldom saw him at all.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲尋包愷，乘一黃牛，被以蒲韉，仍將《漢書》一帙掛於角上，一手捉牛靷，一手翻卷書讀之。

translations.literal: Once when he wished to visit Bao Kai, he rode a yellow ox, covered it with a rush mat, and still hung a bundle of the Book of Han from its horn; with one hand he gripped the ox's reins, with the other he turned the scroll and read.
translations.idiomatic: Once, intending to call on Bao Kai, he rode a yellow ox covered with a rush mat, hung a volume of the Book of Han from its horn, held the reins in one hand, and turned the pages with the other as he rode.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、越國公楊素見於道，從後按轡躡之，既及，問曰：「何處書生，耽學若此？

translations.literal: Yang Su, Duke of Yue and Director of the Department of State Affairs, saw him on the road, pressed his saddle from behind and followed until he caught up, and asked: "What scholar is this, so addicted to study?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su, Duke of Yue and Director of State Affairs, saw him on the road, followed close behind gripping his saddle, and when he had caught up asked, "What sort of student is this, so lost in his books?

sentences.zh: 」密識越公，乃下牛再拜，自言姓名。

translations.literal: " Mi recognized the Duke of Yue, dismounted from the ox, bowed twice, and gave his name.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi recognized the Duke of Yue, dismounted, made a double bow, and stated his name.

sentences.zh: 又問所讀書，答曰《項羽傳》。

translations.literal: Asked what book he was reading, he answered the Biography of Xiang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When asked what he was reading, he replied, the Biography of Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 越公奇之，與語，大悅，謂其子玄感等曰：「吾觀李密識度，汝等不及。

translations.literal: The Duke of Yue marveled at him; conversing with him, he was greatly pleased and said to his son Xuangan and the others: "In my view Li Mi's breadth of understanding—you none of you can match it.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Yue was struck by him; after talking with him he was greatly pleased and told his son Xuangan and the rest, "Judging Li Mi's grasp and vision, none of you can equal him.

sentences.zh: 」於是玄感傾心結托。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xuangan gave him his wholehearted trust and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuangan thereupon pledged himself to Mi with wholehearted trust and friendship.

sentences.zh: 大業九年，煬帝伐高麗，使玄感于黎陽監運。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daye the Emperor Yang campaigned against Goguryeo and sent Xuangan to supervise transport at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Daye, while Emperor Yang campaigned against Goguryeo, he sent Xuangan to oversee transport at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 時天下騷動，玄感將謀舉兵，潛遣人入關迎密，以為謀主。

translations.literal: The realm was in turmoil; Xuangan was about to plot rebellion and secretly sent men into the passes to fetch Mi as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire in turmoil, Xuangan prepared to raise arms and secretly sent men through the passes to bring Mi as his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 密至，謂玄感曰：「今天子出征，遠在遼外，地去幽州，懸隔千里，南有巨海之限，北有胡戎之患，中間一道，理極艱危。

translations.literal: When Mi arrived he said to Xuangan: "Today the Son of Heaven is on campaign, far in Liaodong; the distance to Youzhou is a thousand li of separation. To the south is the great sea's barrier, to the north the trouble of the Hu and Rong; the route between is in the utmost peril.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi arrived he told Xuangan, "The Son of Heaven is on campaign in distant Liaodong, a thousand li from Youzhou; the sea blocks the south, barbarian troubles press the north, and the single road between is desperately hazardous.

sentences.zh: 今公擁兵出其不意，長驅入薊，直扼其喉。

translations.literal: Now if you take your troops by surprise, drive straight into Ji, and seize the throat directly.
translations.idiomatic: If you march in suddenly, drive deep into Ji, and seize their throat directly,

sentences.zh: 前有高麗，退無歸路，不過旬朔，齎糧必盡。

translations.literal: Goguryeo lies ahead, retreat has no road; within ten days or a fortnight their provisions will surely be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: with Goguryeo in front and no way back, within a fortnight their supplies will run out.

sentences.zh: 舉麾一召，其眾自降，不戰而擒，此計之上也。

translations.literal: Raise the banner and summon once—their masses will surrender of themselves; you capture them without fighting. This is the upper plan.
translations.idiomatic: Raise your standard and they will submit without a battle—that is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 關中四塞，天府之國，有衛文升，不足為意。

translations.literal: Within the Passes the land is closed on four sides, a storehouse realm; there is only Wei Wensheng—he is not worth minding.
translations.idiomatic: The Guanzhong heartland is a four-sided fortress and the empire's granary; Wei Wensheng alone is no cause for concern.

sentences.zh: 若經城勿攻，西入長安，掩其無備，天子雖還，失其襟帶。

translations.literal: If you pass cities without attacking, enter Chang'an from the west, and strike while they are unprepared, though the Son of Heaven returns, he loses his collar and belt.
translations.idiomatic: If you bypass the cities without assault, push west into Chang'an while they are unready, then even when the emperor returns he will have lost his strategic belt.

sentences.zh: 據險臨之，固當必克，萬全之勢，此計之中也。

translations.literal: Hold the defiles and press them—you will surely take it; this is a posture of complete security. This is the middle plan.
translations.idiomatic: Seize the passes and press down on them and victory is assured—that is the middling plan.

sentences.zh: 若隨近逐便，先向東都，頓堅城之下，勝負殊未可知，此計之下也。

translations.literal: If you follow what is near and seize convenience, heading first for the Eastern Capital and halting beneath stout walls, victory or defeat is quite unknown—this is the lower plan.
translations.idiomatic: If you take the easy road first toward the Eastern Capital and camp beneath its strong walls, the outcome is anyone's guess—that is the worst plan.

sentences.zh: 」玄感曰：「公之下計，乃上策也。

translations.literal: " Xuangan said: "Your lower plan is in fact the upper strategy.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuangan said, "Your worst plan is actually the best strategy.

sentences.zh: 今百官家口，並在東都，若不取之，安能動物？

translations.literal: Now the families of all officials are in the Eastern Capital; if we do not take it, how can we stir men's hearts?
translations.idiomatic: The households of the entire bureaucracy are in the Eastern Capital; unless we seize it, how can we move men's hearts?

sentences.zh: 且經城不拔，何以示威？

translations.literal: Moreover, if we pass a city without capturing it, how can we display our might?
translations.idiomatic: And if we leave a city untaken on our march, how will we show our power?

sentences.zh: 」密計遂不行。

translations.literal: " Mi's plan was therefore not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi's counsel was set aside.

sentences.zh: 玄感既至東都，頻戰皆捷，自謂天下回應，功在朝夕。

translations.literal: Once Xuangan reached the Eastern Capital he won battle after battle and believed the realm would answer him—that success was within days.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuangan reached the Eastern Capital he won repeated victories and convinced himself the empire would rally to him and triumph was only days away.

sentences.zh: 及獲內史舍人韋福嗣，又委以腹心，是以軍旅之事，不專歸密。

translations.literal: When he captured the Secretariat Gentleman Wei Fusi he again entrusted him with his inner counsels, so that military affairs no longer rested solely with Mi.
translations.idiomatic: When he captured the Secretariat Gentleman Wei Fusi he made him another intimate adviser, and military affairs no longer rested solely with Mi.

sentences.zh: 福嗣既非同謀，因戰被執，每設籌畫，皆持兩端。

translations.literal: Fusi was not a fellow conspirator; captured in battle, whenever he offered plans he hedged on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Fusi was no confederate—he had been taken in battle—and whenever he offered counsel he kept one foot on each side.

sentences.zh: 玄感後使作檄文，福嗣固辭不肯，密揣其情，因謂玄感曰：「福嗣既非同盟，實懷觀望。

translations.literal: Later Xuangan had him draft a proclamation; Fusi firmly refused. Mi gauged his mind and therefore said to Xuangan: "Fusi is no ally and truly harbors a wait-and-see attitude.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xuangan ordered him to draft a proclamation, but Fusi refused outright. Reading his intentions, Mi told Xuangan, "Fusi is no ally; he is really waiting to see which way fortune turns.

sentences.zh: 明公初起大事，而奸人在側，必為所誤，請斬之以謝眾，方可安輯。

translations.literal: My lord has just raised a great affair, yet a traitor is at your side—you will surely be misled by him. I beg you execute him to answer the host and only then can you be secure.
translations.idiomatic: You have just launched a great enterprise with a traitor at your elbow; he is bound to ruin you. Execute him to satisfy the army, and only then will affairs settle.

sentences.zh: 」玄感曰：「何至於此！

translations.literal: " Xuangan said: "How could it come to that!
translations.idiomatic: " Xuangan said, "Surely it need not go that far!

sentences.zh: 」密知言之不用，退謂所親曰：「楚公好反而不圖勝，如何？

translations.literal: " Mi knew his words would not be used. Withdrawing he said to those close to him: "The Duke of Chu loves turning back and does not plan for victory—what then?
translations.idiomatic: " Knowing his advice would be ignored, Mi withdrew and told his intimates, "The Duke of Chu delights in reversal and will not plan for victory—what then?

sentences.zh: 吾屬今為虜矣！

translations.literal: We are captives now!
translations.idiomatic: We are prisoners already!

sentences.zh: 」後玄感將西入，福嗣竟亡歸東都。

translations.literal: " Later when Xuangan was about to march west, Fusi in the end fled back to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xuangan later prepared to march west, Fusi escaped and returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 隋左武衛大將軍李子雄坐事被收，系送行在所，于路殺使者，亡投玄感，乃勸玄感速稱尊號。

translations.literal: The Sui General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard Li Zixiong was arrested for an offense and escorted to the imperial camp; on the road he killed the escort and fled to Xuangan, then urged Xuangan to assume the imperial title at once.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zixiong, Sui General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard, was arrested for an offense and sent under guard toward the emperor's camp; on the road he killed his escort, fled to Xuangan, and urged him to proclaim himself emperor at once.

sentences.zh: 玄感問於密，密曰：「昔陳勝自欲稱王，張耳諫而被外；

translations.literal: Xuangan asked Mi, who said: "Formerly Chen Sheng wished to style himself king; Zhang Er remonstrated and was cast out;
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan asked Mi, who said, "Chen Sheng once wanted to proclaim himself king; Zhang Er remonstrated and was pushed aside;

sentences.zh: 魏武將求九錫，荀彧止而見疏。

translations.literal: Wei Wu was about to seek the Nine Bestowals; Xun Yu stopped him and was distanced.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was about to seek the Nine Bestowals; Xun Yu opposed it and was estranged.

sentences.zh: 今者密若正言，還恐追蹤二子；

translations.literal: if now Mi speaks straight, I still fear following in the tracks of those two;
translations.idiomatic: If I speak plainly now, I may yet follow in their footsteps;

sentences.zh: 阿諛順意，又非密之本圖。

translations.literal: to flatter and comply with his wish is again not Mi's original intent.
translations.idiomatic: yet to flatter and agree with you is not my intent either.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 兵起已來，雖復頻捷，至於郡縣，未有從者。

translations.literal: Since the army rose, though you have won repeatedly, as for commanderies and counties, none have followed.
translations.idiomatic: Since you raised arms you have won battles, yet not a single commandery or county has joined you.

sentences.zh: 東都守禦尚強，天下救兵益至。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital's defense is still strong, and relief armies from across the realm arrive daily.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital's defenses remain strong, and relief armies from across the empire keep arriving.

sentences.zh: 公當身先士眾，早定關中，乃欲急自尊崇，何示人不廣也！

translations.literal: You ought to lead the troops in person and secure Guanzhong early—yet you wish hastily to exalt yourself. What narrowness do you show men!
translations.idiomatic: You should lead the troops yourself and secure Guanzhong quickly, yet you rush to elevate yourself—what a cramped vision you show the world!

sentences.zh: 」玄感笑而止。

translations.literal: " Xuangan laughed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuangan laughed and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 及隋將宇文述、來護兒等率軍且至，玄感謂曰：「計將安出？

translations.literal: When the Sui generals Yuwen Shu, Lai Huer, and others led armies and were about to arrive, Xuangan said: "What plan shall we adopt?
translations.idiomatic: When Sui generals Yuwen Shu, Lai Huer, and others were marching up with their armies, Xuangan asked, "What is our next move?

sentences.zh: 」密曰：「元弘嗣統強兵於隴右，今可陽言其反，遣使迎公，因此入關，可得紿眾。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "Yuan Hongsi commands strong troops in Longyou; now we can falsely announce that he has rebelled and send envoys to welcome you. By this means enter the passes and we can deceive the host.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi said, "Yuan Hongsi commands strong forces in Longyou. Announce falsely that he has rebelled and send envoys to summon you; march into the passes on that pretext and you can deceive the troops.

sentences.zh: 」因引軍西入。

translations.literal: " He therefore led the army westward.
translations.idiomatic: " He then marched the army west.

sentences.zh: 至陝縣，欲圍弘農宮，密諫之曰：「公今詐眾西入，事宜在速，況乃追兵將至，安可稽留！

translations.literal: Reaching Shaan County he wished to besiege the Hongnong Palace. Mi remonstrated: "You now deceive the host to march west—the affair demands speed, and moreover pursuing troops are about to arrive; how can you linger!
translations.idiomatic: At Shaan County he wanted to besiege Hongnong Palace. Mi urged, "You have deceived the army into marching west; speed is everything, and pursuers are close—how can you delay?

sentences.zh: 若前不得據關，退無所守，大眾一散，何以自全？

translations.literal: If ahead you cannot hold the passes and behind there is nothing to defend, once the great host disperses, how will you preserve yourself?
translations.idiomatic: If you fail to seize the passes ahead with no refuge behind, the army will scatter—how will you save yourself?

sentences.zh: 」玄感不從，遂圍之，三日不拔，方引而西。

translations.literal: " Xuangan did not follow; he besieged it, and after three days without taking it, only then marched west.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuangan refused, laid siege for three days without success, and only then marched on west.

sentences.zh: 至於晙鄉，追兵遂及，玄感敗。

translations.literal: At Xunxiang the pursuers caught up and Xuangan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Xunxiang the pursuers overtook him and Xuangan was defeated.

sentences.zh: 密乃間行入關，為捕者所獲。

translations.literal: Mi then entered the passes by hidden routes and was seized by captors.
translations.idiomatic: Mi slipped into the passes by back roads and was captured.

sentences.zh: 時煬帝在高陽，密與其黨俱送帝所，謂其徒曰：「吾等之命，同於朝露，若至高陽，必為俎醢。

translations.literal: The Emperor Yang was then at Gaoyang; Mi and his fellows were all sent to the emperor's presence. He said to his companions: "Our lives are like morning dew; if we reach Gaoyang we will surely be minced meat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang was at Gaoyang, and Mi and his companions were escorted toward him. He told his followers, "Our lives are like dew at dawn; if we reach Gaoyang we will be carved on the block.

sentences.zh: 今在道中，猶可為計，安得行就鼎鑊，不規逃避也！

translations.literal: Now on the road we can still make plans—how can we walk straight into the cauldron and not scheme escape!
translations.idiomatic: We are still on the road and can still act—why march straight into the cauldron without planning escape?

sentences.zh: 」眾然之。

translations.literal: " The crowd agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " They all agreed.

sentences.zh: 其多有金者，密令出示使者曰：「吾等死日，幸用相瘞，其餘即皆報德。

translations.literal: Those among them who had much gold—Mi had them show it to the escorts, saying: "On the day of our death, please use it to bury us; the rest will all repay your kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had gold Mi had display it to the escorts, saying, "When we die, use this to bury us properly; the rest is yours in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 」使者利其金，許之。

translations.literal: " The escorts coveted the gold and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Greedy for the gold, the escorts agreed.

sentences.zh: 及出關外，防禁漸弛，密請市酒食，每夜宴飲，喧嘩竟夕，使者不以為意。

translations.literal: Once outside the passes the guard gradually slackened; Mi asked to buy wine and food, and each night they feasted and drank, noisy until dawn—the escorts paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the passes the guard grew lax; Mi bought wine and food, and they feasted noisily every night until dawn while the escorts took no notice.

sentences.zh: 行至邯鄲，密等七人穿牆而遁。

translations.literal: When they reached Handan, Mi and six others broke through a wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Handan, Mi and six others broke through a wall and escaped.

sentences.zh: 抵平原賊帥郝孝德，孝德不甚禮之。

translations.literal: They reached the Pingyuan bandit chief Hao Xiaode; Xiaode did not treat him with much courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: They came to the Pingyuan bandit leader Hao Xiaode, who received him without much respect.

sentences.zh: 密又舍去，詣淮陽，隱姓名，自稱劉智遠，聚徒教授。

translations.literal: Mi again left him, went to Huaiyang, concealed his name, styled himself Liu Zhiyuan, and gathered disciples to teach.
translations.idiomatic: Mi left again for Huaiyang, hid his identity under the name Liu Zhiyuan, and gathered students to teach.

sentences.zh: 經數月，鬱鬱不得志，為五言詩曰：「金風蕩初節，玉露凋晚林。

translations.literal: After several months, depressed and unfulfilled, he composed a five-character poem: "The golden wind stirs the season's first turn; jade dew withers the late woods.
translations.idiomatic: After several months of frustration he wrote a pentasyllabic poem: "Golden wind shakes the season's first turn; jade dew withers the late woods.

sentences.zh: 此夕窮途士，郁陶傷寸心。

translations.literal: This night a man at the road's end—anguish wounds his inch of heart.
translations.idiomatic: Tonight a man at the end of the road—grief wounds his every inch of heart.

sentences.zh: 野平葭葦合，村荒藜藿深。

translations.literal: The wilds level, reeds and rushes merge; the village desolate, pigweed and beans grow deep.
translations.idiomatic: Level wilds where reeds and rushes merge; deserted villages where pigweed runs deep.

sentences.zh: 眺聽良多感，徙倚獨沾襟。

translations.literal: Gazing and listening bring many feelings; pacing alone, his lapels are soaked.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing and listening stir deep feeling; pacing alone, he soaks his collar.

sentences.zh: 沾襟何所為？

translations.literal: Why soak the lapels?
translations.idiomatic: Why do the lapels grow wet?

sentences.zh: 悵然懷古意。

translations.literal: Sadly he harbors thoughts of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Because ancient longings weigh on him.

sentences.zh: 秦俗猶未平，漢道將何冀？

translations.literal: Qin ways are still unrestored—what can the Han path hope for?
translations.idiomatic: Qin tyranny is not yet ended—what hope is there for Han restoration?

sentences.zh: 樊噲市井徒，蕭何刀筆吏。

translations.literal: Fan Kuai was a market-place fellow; Xiao He a clerk with knife and brush.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kuai was a market brawler; Xiao He a petty clerk with brush and knife.

sentences.zh: 一朝時運會，千古傳名諡。

translations.literal: In one morning the times and fortune met—for a thousand ages their posthumous names are handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the moment turned they won posthumous fame for a thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 寄言世上雄，虛生真可愧。

translations.literal: I send word to the heroes of the world: to live in vain is truly shameful.
translations.idiomatic: I tell the world's bold spirits: to live empty-handed is shame indeed.

sentences.zh: 」詩成而泣下數行。

translations.literal: " When the poem was finished he wept several lines of tears.
translations.idiomatic: " When he finished the poem, tears ran down his face in streams.

sentences.zh: 時人有怪之者，以告太守趙佗，下縣捕之，密又亡去。

translations.literal: Someone who found him strange reported to the prefect Zhao Tuo; the county was ordered to arrest him, and Mi fled again.
translations.idiomatic: Someone who thought him odd reported him to Prefect Zhao Tuo; the county sent men to arrest him, and Mi fled once more.

sentences.zh: 會東郡賊帥翟讓聚黨萬餘人，密往歸之。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhai Rang, bandit chief of Dong Commandery, had gathered a party of more than ten thousand; Mi went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: About then Zhai Rang, a bandit leader of Dong Commandery, had gathered more than ten thousand followers, and Mi went to join him.

sentences.zh: 或有知密是玄感亡將，潛勸讓害之，讓囚密于營外。

translations.literal: Some who knew Mi was Xuangan's fugitive general secretly urged Rang to kill him; Rang imprisoned Mi outside the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Some who knew he was Xuangan's fugitive general secretly urged Rang to kill him, and Rang had Mi imprisoned outside the camp.

sentences.zh: 密因王伯當以策於讓曰：「當今主昏於上，人怨於下，銳兵盡於遼東，和親絕于突厥，方乃巡遊揚、越，委棄京都，此亦劉、項奮起之會，以足下之雄才大略，士馬精勇，席捲二京，誅暴滅虐，則隋氏之不足亡也。

translations.literal: Through Wang Bodang, Mi offered Rang a stratagem: "Today the ruler is benighted above and the people resentful below; crack troops are exhausted in Liaodong, peace-by-marriage with the Turks is broken, and he is touring Yang and Yue, abandoning the capital—this too is the moment when Liu and Xiang rose. With your heroic talent and grand design, troops and horses elite and brave, you could sweep the two capitals, punish the cruel and end tyranny—then the house of Sui would not be hard to destroy.
translations.idiomatic: Through Wang Bodang, Mi laid out a plan for Rang: "The ruler is benighted above and the people resentful below; elite troops are spent in Liaodong, ties with the Turks are broken, and he tours Yang and Yue while abandoning the capital—this is the same moment when Liu Bang and Xiang Yu rose. With your talent and daring, your fierce soldiers and horses, you could sweep both capitals, punish cruelty, and end tyranny, and the Sui would not be hard to overthrow.

sentences.zh: 」讓深加敬慕，遽釋之。

translations.literal: " Rang deeply admired him and at once released him.
translations.idiomatic: " Rang was deeply impressed and released him at once.

sentences.zh: 遣說諸小賊，所至皆降。

translations.literal: He sent him to persuade the lesser bandits; wherever he went they all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was sent to win over smaller bands, and wherever he went they submitted.

sentences.zh: 密又說讓曰：「今兵眾既多，糧無所出，若曠日持久，則人馬困弊，大敵一臨，死亡無日矣！

translations.literal: Mi again urged Rang: "Now the host is already large but grain has no source; if days drag on, men and horses will be worn out—when a great enemy arrives, death will be a matter of no days!
translations.idiomatic: Mi urged Rang again: "Your force is large but there is no grain supply; if this drags on, men and horses will be exhausted, and when a major enemy arrives you will have no days left to live.

sentences.zh: 未若直取滎陽，休兵館穀，待士勇馬肥，然後與人爭利。

translations.literal: Better to strike straight for Xingyang, rest the troops and store grain, wait until soldiers are brave and horses fat, and only then contend with others for advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Better march straight on Xingyang, rest the troops, and stock grain; when your men are bold and your horses strong, then fight for mastery.

sentences.zh: 」讓以為然。

translations.literal: " Rang thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: " Rang agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是破金堤關，掠滎陽諸縣城堡，多下之。

translations.literal: From this they broke the Jindi Pass and raided the fortified places of Xingyang's counties—many fell.
translations.idiomatic: They then stormed Jindi Pass and seized fortified places throughout Xingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 滎陽太宗楊慶及通守張須陀以兵討讓，讓曾為須陀所敗，聞其來，大懼，將遠避之。

translations.literal: Yang Qing, Prince of Zheng in Xingyang, and the transit governor Zhang Xutuo led troops against Rang; Rang had once been defeated by Xutuo—hearing of his coming, he was greatly afraid and was about to flee far off.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing, Prince of Zheng in Xingyang, and Transit Governor Zhang Xutuo marched against Rang, who had been beaten by Xutuo before; hearing he was coming, Rang was terrified and prepared to flee.

sentences.zh: 密曰：「須陀勇而無謀，兵又驟勝，既驕且狠，可一戰而擒之。

translations.literal: Mi said: "Xutuo is brave but without strategy; his troops have won suddenly and are both arrogant and harsh—we can capture him in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said, "Xutuo is brave but not clever; his troops have won too quickly and are arrogant and cruel—we can take him in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 公但列陣以待，為公破之。

translations.literal: You need only draw up ranks and wait; I will break him for you.
translations.idiomatic: You need only form the line and wait—I will defeat him for you.

sentences.zh: 」讓不得已，勒兵將戰，密分兵千余人于木林間設伏。

translations.literal: " Rang had no choice; he marshaled the troops to fight. Mi detached more than a thousand men to set an ambush in the wooded grove.
translations.idiomatic: " Rang had no choice but to deploy for battle while Mi hid more than a thousand men in the woods.

sentences.zh: 讓與戰不利，稍卻，密發伏自後掩之，須陀眾潰，與讓合擊，大破之，遂斬須陀於陣。

translations.literal: Rang's battle went ill and he drew back slightly; Mi launched the ambush from behind to strike him—Xutuo's host collapsed; joining with Rang they struck together and routed them utterly, and beheaded Xutuo on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Rang's fight went badly and he fell back; Mi's ambush struck from behind, Xutuo's force collapsed, and together they routed the enemy and killed Xutuo in the battle.

sentences.zh: 讓於是令密別統所部。

translations.literal: Rang thereupon had Mi command his own division separately.
translations.idiomatic: Rang then put Mi in independent command of his own force.

sentences.zh: 密軍陣整肅，凡號令兵士，雖盛夏皆若背負霜雪。

translations.literal: Mi's army formations were orderly and stern; whenever he ordered the soldiers, even in midsummer they were as if bearing frost and snow on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's formations were disciplined and stern; his orders were obeyed as if the men carried winter frost on their backs even in midsummer.

sentences.zh: 躬服儉素，所得金寶皆頒賜麾下，由是人為之用。

translations.literal: He personally wore plain thrift; all gold and jewels obtained he distributed to those below, and thereby men acted at his command.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly himself and gave all captured gold and jewels to his men, so they served him willingly.

sentences.zh: 尋復說讓曰：「昏主蒙塵，播蕩吳、越，群兵競起，海內饑荒。

translations.literal: Soon he again urged Rang: "The benighted ruler is lost in dust, roaming Wu and Yue; hosts of soldiers rise in rivalry and famine grips the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he urged Rang again: "The benighted emperor wanders in distress through Wu and Yue; armies rise everywhere and famine grips the land.

sentences.zh: 明公以英傑之才，而統驍雄之旅，宜當廓清天下，誅剪群凶，豈可求食草間，常為小盜而已！

translations.literal: My lord, with heroic talent, commands fierce and valiant hosts—you ought to clear the realm and cut down the wicked. How can you seek food in the grass and remain a petty bandit only!
translations.idiomatic: With your heroic gifts you command fierce troops—you should clear the realm and destroy the wicked, not grub for food in the weeds like a petty bandit forever!

sentences.zh: 今東都士庶，中外離心，留守諸官，政令不一。

translations.literal: Now the gentry and commoners of the Eastern Capital are at odds within and without; the officials left to guard issue no unified orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital's people are divided in heart, and the officials left behind cannot agree on policy.

sentences.zh: 明公親率大眾，直掩興洛倉，發粟以賑窮乏，遠近孰不歸附？

translations.literal: If my lord personally leads the great host straight against the Xingluo granary, opens the grain to relieve the destitute—who near or far would not attach to you?
translations.idiomatic: Lead the host yourself straight against the Xingluo granary, open the grain to feed the destitute—who near or far would not rally to you?

sentences.zh: 百萬之眾，一朝可集，先發制人，此機不可失也！

translations.literal: A host of a million can be gathered in a morning; strike first and control others—this opportunity must not be lost!
translations.idiomatic: A million followers can be gathered in a day; strike first and seize the advantage—this chance must not be missed!

sentences.zh: 」讓曰：「僕起隴畝之間，望不至此，必如所圖，請君先發，僕領諸軍便為後殿。

translations.literal: " Rang said: "I rose from between the furrows and never hoped for this; if it must be as you plan, I beg you march first—I will lead the rest of the army as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: " Rang said, "I came up from the fields and never dreamed of this; if we do as you propose, you go first and I will bring up the rear with the rest of the army.

sentences.zh: 得倉之日，當別議之。

translations.literal: On the day we take the granary we can discuss the rest separately.
translations.idiomatic: Once we hold the granary we can decide the rest.

sentences.zh: 」春，密與讓領精兵千人出陽城北，逾方山，自羅口襲興洛倉，破之。

translations.literal: " In spring Mi and Rang led a thousand elite troops out north of Yangcheng, crossed Fang Mountain, and from Luokou raided the Xingluo granary and took it.
translations.idiomatic: " That spring Mi and Rang led a thousand picked troops out north of Yangcheng, crossed Fang Mountain, struck the Xingluo granary from Luokou, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 開倉恣人所取，老弱繈負，道路不絕，眾至數十萬。

translations.literal: They opened the granary and let people take freely; old and young came on one another's backs, the roads unceasing—the host reached several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the granaries for free taking; the old and weak came on one another's backs without end along the roads, and the following swelled to hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 隋越王侗遣虎賁郎將劉長恭率步騎二萬五千討密，密一戰破之，長恭僅以身免。

translations.literal: The Sui Prince of Yue, Yang Tong, sent the Tiger Guard General Liu Changgong with twenty-five thousand infantry and cavalry against Mi; Mi defeated them in one battle and Changgong barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tong, the Sui Prince of Yue, sent Tiger Guard General Liu Changgong with twenty-five thousand foot and horse to attack Mi; Mi routed them in a single battle, and Changgong barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 讓於是推密為主，號為魏公。

translations.literal: Rang thereupon made Mi their leader, styling him Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Rang then made Mi their leader, with the title Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 二月，于鞏南設壇場，即位，稱元年，其文書行下稱行軍元帥魏公府。

translations.literal: In the second month he set up an altar south of Gong, took the throne, proclaimed the first year of his reign, and documents issued below bore the heading Campaign Marshal, Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he set up an altar south of Gong, took the throne, proclaimed year one, and his documents went out under the title Campaign Marshal, Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 以房彥藻為左長史，邴元真為右長史，楊得方為左司馬，鄭德韜為右司馬。

translations.literal: He appointed Fang Yanzao Left Chief Clerk, Bing Yuanzhen Right Chief Clerk, Yang Defang Left Major, and Zheng Detao Right Major.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Fang Yanzao as Left Chief Clerk, Bing Yuanzhen as Right Chief Clerk, Yang Defang as Left Major, and Zheng Detao as Right Major.

sentences.zh: 拜翟讓為司徒，封東郡公。

translations.literal: He invested Zhai Rang as Minister of Education and enfeoffed him as Duke of Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zhai Rang Minister of Education and enfeoffed him as Duke of Dong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 單雄信為左武候大將軍，徐世勣為右武候大將軍，祖君彥為記室，其餘封拜各有差。

translations.literal: Shan Xiongxin was Left Martial Guard General-in-Chief, Xu Shiji Right Martial Guard General-in-Chief, Zu Junyan Recorder—the rest received ranks and titles in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Xiongxin became Left Martial Guard General-in-Chief, Xu Shiji Right Martial Guard General-in-Chief, and Zu Junyan Recorder; the rest received ranks and titles according to merit.

sentences.zh: 於是城洛口周回四十里以居之。

translations.literal: He then walled Luokou, forty li in circuit, to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: He then fortified Luokou on a circuit of forty li and made it his seat.

sentences.zh: 長白山賊孟讓率所部歸密，鞏縣長柴孝和、侍御史鄭頤以鞏縣降密。

translations.literal: The Changbai Mountain bandit Meng Rang led his following to submit to Mi; Chai Xiaohe, magistrate of Gong County, and the Investigating Censor Zheng Yi surrendered Gong to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: The Changbai bandit Meng Rang brought his force to Mi; Magistrate Chai Xiaohe of Gong and Investigating Censor Zheng Yi surrendered the county.

sentences.zh: 隋虎賁郎將裴仁基率其子行儼以武牢歸密，拜為上柱國，封河東郡公。

translations.literal: The Sui Tiger Guard General Pei Renji led his son Xingyan and surrendered Wulao to Mi; Mi invested him as Superior Pillar of State and enfeoffed him Duke of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Tiger Guard General Pei Renji came over with his son Xingyan and surrendered Wulao; Mi made him Superior Pillar of State and Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 因遣仁基與孟讓率兵三萬餘人襲回洛倉，破之，入東都，俘掠居人，燒天津，東都出兵乘之，仁基等大敗，僅以身免。

translations.literal: He then sent Renji and Meng Rang with more than thirty thousand troops to raid the Huiluo granary; they took it, entered the Eastern Capital, seized and plundered the inhabitants, and burned Tianjin Bridge. The Eastern Capital sent troops to strike while they were exposed; Renji and the rest were utterly defeated and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Renji and Meng Rang with over thirty thousand men to seize the Huiluo granary, then entered the Eastern Capital, plundered the populace, and burned Tianjin Bridge. Capital troops struck at their moment of exposure; Renji's force was shattered and the leaders barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 密復親率兵三萬逼東都，將軍段達、虎賁郎將高毗、劉長林等出兵七萬拒之，戰於故都城，隋軍敗走。

translations.literal: Mi again personally led thirty thousand troops to press the Eastern Capital; the generals Duan Da, the Tiger Guard Generals Gao Pi and Liu Changlin, and others led seventy thousand to resist. They fought at the old capital city and the Sui army fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Mi again led thirty thousand men against the Eastern Capital; General Duan Da, Tiger Guard Generals Gao Pi and Liu Changlin, and others marched out seventy thousand to meet him. At the old capital site the Sui force was routed.

sentences.zh: 密復下回洛倉而據之，大修營塹，以逼東都，仍作書以移郡縣曰：

translations.literal: Mi again descended on the Huiluo granary and held it, greatly repairing ramparts and ditches to press the Eastern Capital, and also composed a letter to the commanderies and counties, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Mi again took the Huiluo granary, threw up extensive fortifications to press the Eastern Capital, and issued a proclamation to the commanderies and counties:

sentences.zh: 「自元氣肇辟，厥初生人，樹之帝王，以為司牧。

translations.literal: " From the time primordial qi first opened the world and mankind first arose, emperors and kings were set up as shepherds of the people.
translations.idiomatic: " From the opening of primordial order and the first arising of mankind, emperors and kings were established to shepherd the people.

sentences.zh: 是以羲、農、軒、頊之后，堯、舜、禹、湯之君，靡不祗畏上玄，愛育黔首，乾乾終日，翼翼小心，馭朽索而同危，履春冰而是懼。

translations.literal: Therefore the successors of Fuxi, Shennong, Xuanyuan, and Zhuanxu, the rulers Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang—none failed to revere Heaven above, cherish and nurture the black-haired people, toil diligently all day, and tread with utmost care, driving a rotted rope as if in equal peril and walking spring ice as if in fear.
translations.idiomatic: The heirs of Fuxi, Shennong, the Yellow Emperor, and Zhuanxu, and the rulers Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang—all revered Heaven, cherished the people, labored diligently, and walked in utmost caution, as if driving a frayed rope over an abyss or treading spring ice.

sentences.zh: 故一物失所，若納隍而愧之；

translations.literal: Thus if one thing lost its place, they felt shame as if falling into a dry moat;
translations.idiomatic: If a single thing went awry they felt ashamed as if plunging into a pit;

sentences.zh: 一夫有罪，遂下車而泣之。

translations.literal: if one man had guilt, they would leave the carriage and weep for him.
translations.idiomatic: if one man was guilty they left the carriage and wept for him.

sentences.zh: 謙德軫於責躬，憂勞切於罪己。

translations.literal: Their modest virtue was shown in blaming themselves; their anxious toil lay in confessing fault.
translations.idiomatic: Their humility showed in self-reproach; their care lay in confessing their own faults.

sentences.zh: 普天之下，率土之濱，蟠木距於流沙，瀚海窮於丹穴，莫不鼓腹擊壤，鑿井耕田，治致升平，驅之仁壽。

translations.literal: Under all Heaven, along the shores of the realm, from twisted trees at the shifting sands to the far reaches of the red grotto, none failed to drum their bellies and strike the earth, dig wells and plow fields, bring order to peace, and drive the people toward benevolence and long life.
translations.idiomatic: Across the realm, from the western wastes to the eastern seas, all drummed their bellies in contentment, dug wells and plowed fields, and were brought to peace and long life under benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 是以愛之如父母，敬之若神明，用能享國多年，祚延長世。

translations.literal: Therefore the people loved them as parents and revered them as spirits, and so they could enjoy the state for many years and extend their fortune through ages.
translations.idiomatic: The people loved them as parents and revered them as gods, and so their reigns lasted many years and their fortunes extended through generations.

sentences.zh: 未有暴虐臨人，克終天位者也。

translations.literal: Never has a tyrant who abused the people been able to finish his heavenly mandate.
translations.idiomatic: No tyrant who abused the people has ever kept the Mandate of Heaven to the end.

sentences.zh: 隋氏往因周末，預奉綴衣，狐媚而圖聖寶，胠篋以取神器。

translations.literal: The house of Sui in former days, at the end of Zhou, received the trailing robe in advance; with fawning craft they plotted for the sacred treasure and broke open coffers to seize the divine regalia.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui clan, at the end of the Zhou, received the imperial robe in advance, fawned their way toward the throne, and broke open the storehouses to seize the regalia of empire.

sentences.zh: 及纘承負扆，狼虎其心，始曀明兩之暉，終干少陽之位。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne with the screen at his back, his heart was that of wolf and tiger; at first he dimmed the radiance of the two suns, and in the end he violated the place of the young yang.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne his heart was wolf and tiger; he first dimmed the light of his father and elder brother, then violated the place of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 先皇大漸，侍疾禁中，遂為梟獍，便行鴆毒。

translations.literal: When the late emperor fell gravely ill, attending his sickness within the palace, he became an owl and a porcupine and administered poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: While the late emperor lay gravely ill in the palace, he played the dutiful son at the bedside and then poisoned his father.

sentences.zh: 禍深於莒僕，釁酷于商臣，天地難容，人神嗟憤！

translations.literal: His calamity was deeper than that of the Ju servant; his outrage fouler than Shang Chen's—Heaven and Earth could not bear him; men and spirits sighed in rage!
translations.idiomatic: His crime outdid the Ju servant's murder and Shang Chen's parricide—Heaven and Earth could not contain him; men and spirits groaned in fury!

sentences.zh: 州吁安忍，閼伯日尋，劍閣所以懷凶，晉陽所以興亂，甸人為罄，淫刑斯逞。

translations.literal: Like Zhou Xu's cruel forbearance and Yan Bo's daily strife, Jian'ge harbored malice and Jinyang rose in disorder; the suburban people were exhausted and licentious punishments ran riot.
translations.idiomatic: Like Zhou Xu's cruelty and Yan Bo's daily feuds, he nursed malice at Jian'ge and stirred rebellion at Jinyang; the people were drained dry and cruel punishments ran unchecked.

sentences.zh: 夫九族既睦，唐帝闡其欽明；

translations.literal: When the nine kindreds are harmonious, the Tang emperor displayed his reverent brilliance;
translations.idiomatic: When the nine clans live in harmony, as under the Tang emperor, reverent brilliance shines forth;

sentences.zh: 百世本枝，文王表其光大。

translations.literal: when the root and branches endure for a hundred generations, King Wen showed their vast radiance.
translations.idiomatic: when root and branch endure for a hundred generations, as under King Wen, their glory is made manifest.

sentences.zh: 況復隳壞磐石，剿絕維城，脣亡齒寒，甯止虞、虢？

translations.literal: How much more when he destroyed the bedrock boulder and exterminated the walling states—when the lips perish the teeth grow cold; does this stop with Yu and Guo alone?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he shattered the bedrock of the realm and destroyed its shielding princes—when the lips are gone the teeth freeze; and this was not limited to the states of Yu and Guo alone.

sentences.zh: 欲其長久，其可得乎！

translations.literal: To wish that such a rule endure long—how could it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: To expect such a house to endure—how could it?

sentences.zh: 其罪一也。

translations.literal: This is his first crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first of his crimes.

sentences.zh: 禽獸之行，在於聚麀，人倫之體，別於內外。

translations.literal: The conduct of birds and beasts lies in gathering mates in confusion; the form of human relations distinguishes inner from outer.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts gather mates without distinction; human relations draw a line between inner and outer kin.

sentences.zh: 而蘭陵公主逼幸告終，誰謂敤首之賢，翻見齊襄之恥。

translations.literal: Yet the Princess of Lanling was forced to his bed until her end—who would call the virtue of the Qi maiden admirable, when instead one sees the shame of Duke Xiang of Qi?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he forced the Princess of Lanling to his bed until her death—what virtue of the Qi maiden could be praised when Qi Xiang's incest stands revealed?

sentences.zh: 逮於先皇嬪御，並進銀環；

translations.literal: Reaching to the late emperor's consorts and attendants, all were brought in with silver rings;
translations.idiomatic: He took even the late emperor's consorts and attendants, each admitted with a silver ring;

sentences.zh: 諸王子女，咸貯金屋。

translations.literal: the sons and daughters of the princes were all stored in golden chambers.
translations.idiomatic: and the sons and daughters of the imperial princes were all locked in golden chambers.

sentences.zh: 牝雞鳴於詰旦，雄雉恣其群飛，衵衣戲陳侯之朝，穹廬同冒頓之寢。

translations.literal: The hen crowed at dawn; the cock pheasant wantoned in flocking flight; in undergarments he sported in Duke Chen's court, in a felt tent he shared Modu's bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: The hen crowed at dawn and the cock flew wild; in his undergarments he played the part of Duke Chen, in a felt tent he shared the bed of Modu.

sentences.zh: 爵賞之出，女謁遂成，公卿宣淫，無復綱紀。

translations.literal: Titles and rewards issued through women's access; dukes and ministers displayed debauchery—no discipline remained.
translations.idiomatic: Rank and reward flowed through women's chambers; ministers openly debauched themselves—and all discipline was gone.

sentences.zh: 其罪二也。

translations.literal: This is his second crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second of his crimes.

sentences.zh: 平章百姓，一日萬機，未曉求衣，昃晷不食。

translations.literal: To settle the affairs of the people, ten thousand matters in a day—before dawn to seek robes, at the slanting sun still not eating.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler settles the people's affairs, ten thousand matters a day—rising before dawn for court, working past sunset without a meal.

sentences.zh: 大禹不貴於尺壁，光武不隔于支體，以是憂勤，深慮幽枉。

translations.literal: Yu the Great did not prize a foot-square jade; Guangwu did not screen his limbs—thus they were anxious and diligent, deeply concerned for hidden wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: Yu the Great did not prize a foot-square jade disk; Emperor Guangwu of Han did not hide behind screens—thus they labored in care and thought deeply on hidden wrongs.

sentences.zh: 而荒湎於酒，俾晝作夜，式號且呼，甘嗜聲伎，常居窟室，每藉糟丘。

translations.literal: Yet he was lost in wine, making day into night, shouting and calling at dawn, delighting in music and performers, constantly dwelling in cellar rooms, always leaning on dregs hills.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he drowned in wine, turned day into night, shouted through the dawn, craved music and performers, lived in cellar rooms, and slept on heaps of lees.

sentences.zh: 朝謁罕見其身，群臣希睹其面，斷決自此不行，敷奏於是停擁。

translations.literal: At court audiences his person was rarely seen; the ministers seldom beheld his face—judgments from then on were not carried out, and memorials thereafter piled up unstopped.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was rarely seen; ministers seldom glimpsed his face—judgments ceased, and memorials piled up unread.

sentences.zh: 中山千日之飲，酩酊無名；

translations.literal: The thousand-day wine of Zhongshan—stupefied without end;
translations.idiomatic: He drank the thousand-day wine of Zhongshan until senseless;

sentences.zh: 襄陽三雅之杯，留連詎比？

translations.literal: the Three Elegances cups of Xiangyang—could lingering compare?
translations.idiomatic: and lingered over the Three Elegances cups of Xiangyang—what comparison is there?

sentences.zh: 又廣召良家，充選宮掖，潛為九市，親駕四驢，自比商人，見要逆旅。

translations.literal: Again he broadly summoned good families to fill the palace women's quarters; secretly he made a ninefold market, personally drove four donkeys, compared himself to merchants, and was detained at roadside inns.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned good families to fill the palace, ran a secret market in nine wards, drove four donkeys himself, played the merchant, and was waylaid at inns like a common traveler.

sentences.zh: 殷辛之譴為小，漢靈之罪更輕，內外驚心，遐邇失望。

translations.literal: The reproach of Yin Xin would be small; the crime of Han Ling would be lighter—within and without hearts were startled; near and far hope was lost.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou's offenses would seem small; Emperor Ling's crimes would seem light—court and country were appalled; near and far lost all hope.

sentences.zh: 其罪三也。

translations.literal: This is his third crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third of his crimes.

sentences.zh: 上棟下宇，著在《易》爻；

translations.literal: Rafters above and walls below are set forth in the lines of the Changes;
translations.idiomatic: Rafters above and walls below are prescribed in the Book of Changes;

sentences.zh: 茅茨采椽，陳諸史籍。

translations.literal: thatched roofs and unplaned rafters are recorded in the historical annals.
translations.idiomatic: thatched roofs and plain rafters are praised in the histories.

sentences.zh: 聖人本意，惟避風雨，詎待朱玉之華，寧須綈錦之麗！

translations.literal: The sages' original intent was only to keep off wind and rain—why wait for the splendor of vermilion and jade, or need the beauty of fine silk brocade!
translations.idiomatic: The sages meant only shelter from wind and rain—why demand vermilion pillars and jade doors, or brocade splendor!

sentences.zh: 故璿室崇構，商辛以之滅亡；

translations.literal: Therefore the lofty Jade Chamber—Shang Xin perished by it;
translations.idiomatic: The towering Jade Chamber brought the fall of King Zhou;

sentences.zh: 阿房崛起，二世是以傾覆。

translations.literal: Epang rose in grandeur—the Second Emperor was overturned thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Epang Palace's rise brought down the Second Emperor.

sentences.zh: 而不遵古典，不念前章，廣立池臺，多營宮觀，金鋪玉戶，青瑣丹墀，蔽虧日月，隔閡寒暑。

translations.literal: Yet he did not follow ancient models or heed former warnings; he broadly raised pools and towers and built many palaces and halls—golden studs, jade doors, green lattice, cinnabar steps—blocking sun and moon and shutting out cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he ignored ancient models and former warnings, raised pools and towers everywhere, and built palaces with golden studs, jade doors, green lattice, and cinnabar steps that blocked out sun and season alike.

sentences.zh: 窮生人之筋力，罄天下之資財，使鬼尚難為之，勞人固其不可。

translations.literal: He exhausted living men's sinew and bone and drained the realm's wealth—even ghosts would find it hard to accomplish, and to weary men was surely impossible.
translations.idiomatic: He exhausted men's strength and drained the empire's wealth—work even ghosts could scarcely finish, and labor men could not bear.

sentences.zh: 其罪四也。

translations.literal: This is his fourth crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth of his crimes.

sentences.zh: 公田所徹，不過十畝；

translations.literal: What was levied from the public fields did not exceed ten mu;
translations.idiomatic: Levies from the public fields did not exceed ten mu;

sentences.zh: 人力所供，才止三日。

translations.literal: what human labor supplied stopped at three days.
translations.idiomatic: and labor service was limited to three days.

sentences.zh: 是以輕徭薄賦，不奪農時，甯積於人，無藏於府。

translations.literal: Therefore corvée was light and taxes thin, the farming seasons were not seized, wealth was stored among the people, and nothing was hoarded in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Thus corvée was light, taxes were low, the seasons were not disturbed, wealth stayed with the people, and the treasury was not stuffed.

sentences.zh: 而科稅繁猥，不知紀極；

translations.literal: Yet his tax categories were numerous and tangled, without limit or end;
translations.idiomatic: Yet his taxes multiplied beyond reckoning;

sentences.zh: 猛火屢燒，漏卮難滿。

translations.literal: fierce fires burned again and again, and a leaking goblet could not be filled.
translations.idiomatic: fierce exactions burned again and again, and the treasury was a leaking cup that could never be filled.

sentences.zh: 頭會箕斂，逆折十年之租；

translations.literal: Head by head they met and swept with winnowing baskets, seizing ten years' rent in advance;
translations.idiomatic: Collectors gathered grain head by head and swept up ten years' rent in advance;

sentences.zh: 杼軸其空，日損千金之費。

translations.literal: shuttles and looms stood empty, and a thousand in gold was lost each day.
translations.idiomatic: looms stood empty in every household, and a thousand in gold was lost each day.

sentences.zh: 父母不保其赤子，夫妻相棄于匡床。

translations.literal: Parents could not keep their infants; husbands and wives abandoned one another on the marriage bed.
translations.idiomatic: Parents could not keep their children; husbands and wives abandoned one another in their own beds.

sentences.zh: 萬戶則城郭空虛，千里則煙火斷滅。

translations.literal: Ten thousand households left cities and towns empty; for a thousand li cooking smoke was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand households left the cities empty; for a thousand li hearth-fires went out.

sentences.zh: 西蜀王孫之室，翻同原憲之貧；

translations.literal: The chambers of Western Shu princes turned poor as Yuan Xian's;
translations.idiomatic: The mansions of Western Shu princes became as poor as Yuan Xian's hovel;

sentences.zh: 東海糜竺之家，俄成鄧通之鬼。

translations.literal: the house of Mi Zhu of Donghai soon became the ghost of Deng Tong.
translations.idiomatic: the house of Mi Zhu in the eastern sea soon joined Deng Tong among the dead.

sentences.zh: 其罪五也。

translations.literal: This is his fifth crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth of his crimes.

sentences.zh: 古先哲王，卜征巡狩，唐、虞五載，周則一紀。

translations.literal: The sage kings of antiquity divined before campaigns and tours of inspection—Tang and Yu once in five years, Zhou once in twelve.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of old divined before tours of inspection—once in five years under Yao and Shun, once in twelve under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 本欲親問疾苦，觀省風謠，乃復廣積薪芻，多備饔餼。

translations.literal: They meant personally to inquire into suffering and observe local songs—yet he again piled fuel and fodder broadly and prepared feasts in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to ask after the people's hardships and hear local songs—yet he piled up fodder everywhere and prepared lavish provisions.

sentences.zh: 年年曆覽，處處登臨，從臣疲弊，供頓辛苦。

translations.literal: Year after year he toured and viewed; place after place he climbed and looked—followers were worn out, supplies and halts were bitter toil.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he toured; place after place he climbed—his followers were exhausted and every halt was misery.

sentences.zh: 飄風凍雨，聊竊比于先驅；

translations.literal: Gusting wind and freezing rain—he could only compare himself to the vanguard;
translations.idiomatic: Wind and freezing rain—he could only liken himself to the vanguard;

sentences.zh: 車轍馬跡，遂周行於天下。

translations.literal: cart ruts and horse tracks circled the realm.
translations.idiomatic: cart tracks and hoofprints circled the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 秦皇之心未已，周穆之意難窮。

translations.literal: The heart of Qin Shi Huang was not yet satisfied; the intent of King Mu of Zhou was hard to exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: The ambition of the First Emperor of Qin was not yet sated; the wanderlust of King Mu of Zhou could not be exhausted.

sentences.zh: 宴西母而歌雲，浮東海而觀日。

translations.literal: He feasted the Queen Mother of the West and sang of clouds; he floated the eastern sea to watch the sun.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted the Queen Mother of the West and sang among the clouds; he sailed the eastern sea to watch the sunrise.

sentences.zh: 家苦納秸之勤，人阻來蘇之望。

translations.literal: Households were bitter from supplying straw; the people's hope of returning to life was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Households groaned under the levy of fodder; the people's hope of relief was cut off.

sentences.zh: 且夫天下有道，守在海外，夷不亂華，在德非險。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the realm has the Way, defense lies beyond the seas; barbarians do not disturb the Hua—security lies in virtue, not in passes.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm holds the Way, defense lies beyond the frontier; barbarians do not disturb China—security rests on virtue, not on walls.

sentences.zh: 長城之役，戰國所為，乃是狙詐之風，非關稽古之法。

translations.literal: The labor on the Long Wall was the work of the Warring States—it was the fashion of crafty deceit, not a method traced to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The Long Wall was a Warring States project—the fashion of crafty states, not a method sanctioned by antiquity.

sentences.zh: 而追蹤秦代，板築更興，襲其基墟，延袤萬里，屍骸蔽野，血流成河，積怨滿於山川，號哭動於天地。

translations.literal: Yet he followed the track of Qin, raised rammed-earth works again, took up their ruined foundations, and extended them ten thousand li—corpses covered the wilds, blood flowed like a river, piled resentment filled mountains and streams, and wailing moved Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he followed Qin's example, raised the rammed-earth works again, and extended them ten thousand li—corpses covered the fields, blood ran like rivers, resentment filled the hills, and wailing shook Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 其罪六也。

translations.literal: This is his sixth crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth of his crimes.

sentences.zh: 遼水之東，朝鮮之地，《禹貢》以為荒服，周王棄而不臣，示以羈縻，達其聲教，苟欲愛人，非求拓土。

translations.literal: East of the Liao River lies the land of Joseon—the Tribute of Yu counts it as distant service; the Zhou king abandoned it and did not make it a subject, showing only loose reins to extend civilizing influence; if one wishes to cherish men, one does not seek to expand territory.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Liao lies Korea—the Yu Gong treats it as outer domain; the Zhou king left it unsubdued, holding it only by loose reins to spread civilization—if one loves the people, one does not seek new territory.

sentences.zh: 又強弩末矢，理無穿于魯縞；

translations.literal: Moreover, a strong crossbow at its last shot—by principle it cannot pierce a Lu silk gauze;
translations.idiomatic: A strong crossbow's last bolt cannot pierce a Lu gauze;

sentences.zh: 沖風餘力，詎能動於鴻毛？

translations.literal: the remnant force of a rushing wind—how could it stir a goose feather?
translations.idiomatic: the tail of a gale cannot stir a goose feather—

sentences.zh: 石田得而無堪，雞肋啖而何用？

translations.literal: stony fields may be gained but are unusable; chicken ribs may be eaten—but what use are they?
translations.idiomatic: stony fields gained are useless; chicken ribs eaten are profitless.

sentences.zh: 而恃眾怙力，強兵黷武，惟在併吞，不思長策。

translations.literal: Yet relying on numbers and trusting in force, he fed strong armies and abused war, thinking only of swallowing up, never of long-term plans.
translations.idiomatic: Yet trusting in numbers and force, he fed armies and abused war, thinking only of conquest and never of lasting strategy.

sentences.zh: 夫兵，猶火也；

translations.literal: War is like fire;
translations.idiomatic: War is like fire;

sentences.zh: 不戢，將自焚，遂令億兆夷人，只輪莫返。

translations.literal: if not restrained it will burn the wielder—thus he caused millions of common folk in the eastern campaigns not one cartwheel to return.
translations.idiomatic: unchecked it burns the wielder—so millions marched east and not a single wheel returned.

sentences.zh: 夫差喪國，實為黃池之盟；

translations.literal: Fuchai lost his state—it was truly because of the alliance at Huangchi;
translations.idiomatic: Fuchai lost his kingdom at the alliance of Huangchi;

sentences.zh: 苻堅滅身，良由壽春之役。

translations.literal: Fu Jian destroyed himself—it was indeed because of the campaign at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian destroyed himself at the campaign of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 欲捕鳴蟬於前，不知挾彈在後。

translations.literal: He wished to catch the chirping cicada ahead and did not know the slingshot bearer behind.
translations.idiomatic: He reached for the cicada in front and did not see the slingshot behind.

sentences.zh: 復矢相顧，髽而成行，義夫切齒，壯士扼腕。

translations.literal: Veterans looked back on one another, mourning queues in rows; men of honor ground their teeth, stalwarts clutched their wrists.
translations.idiomatic: Veterans looked back in mourning queues; righteous men ground their teeth and heroes clenched their fists.

sentences.zh: 其罪七也。

translations.literal: This is his seventh crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh of his crimes.

sentences.zh: 直言啟沃，王臣匪躬，惟木從繩，若金須礪。

translations.literal: Straight words open the mind; a king's minister is not for himself alone—only wood follows the line, as metal must be honed.
translations.idiomatic: Straight counsel opens the ruler's mind; a loyal minister serves not himself—wood must follow the line, metal must be honed.

sentences.zh: 唐堯建鼓，思聞獻替之言；

translations.literal: Tang of Yao set up a drum, desiring to hear words of correction and replacement;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yao set up a drum, eager to hear counsel for improvement;

sentences.zh: 夏禹懸鞀，時聽箴規之美。

translations.literal: Yu of Xia hung a sounding stone, often listening to the beauty of admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Yu of Xia hung a sounding stone, often listening to admonition.

sentences.zh: 而愎諫違卜，蠹賢嫉能，直士正人，皆由屠害。

translations.literal: Yet he was obstinate toward remonstrance and defied divination, harmed the worthy and envied ability—upright men and correct persons were all put to the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was deaf to remonstrance, defied divination, harmed the worthy and envied talent—upright men were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 左僕射、齊國公高穎，上柱國、宋國公賀若弼，或文昌上相，或細柳功臣，暫吐良藥之言，翻加屬鏤之賜。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director, Duke of Qi Gao Jiong, and Superior Pillar of State, Duke of Song He Ruobi—one a chief minister of the civil constellation, one a meritorious minister of Xiliu—briefly spoke healing words yet were instead given the gift of the gilded awl.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, Duke of Qi, and Superior Pillar He Ruobi, Duke of Song—one a chief minister, one a hero of Xiliu—offered bitter counsel and received the gilded awl in reward.

sentences.zh: 龍逢無罪，便遭夏癸之誅；

translations.literal: Long Feng was without guilt yet met the execution of Xia Gui;
translations.idiomatic: Long Feng was innocent yet was executed by Jie of Xia;

sentences.zh: 王子何辜？

translations.literal: What guilt had the princes?
translations.idiomatic: What crime had the princes committed?

sentences.zh: 濫被商辛之戮。

translations.literal: They were wantonly subjected to the slaughter of Shang Xin.
translations.idiomatic: They were slaughtered like victims of King Zhou.

sentences.zh: 遂令君子結舌，賢人緘口。

translations.literal: Thus gentlemen bit their tongues and worthies sealed their lips.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen fell silent and worthies sealed their lips.

sentences.zh: 指白日而比盛，射蒼天而敢欺，不悟國之將亡，不知死之將至。

translations.literal: He pointed at the bright sun and compared his splendor; he shot at the blue sky and dared to deceive—he did not realize the state was about to perish, did not know death was about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: He swore by the bright sun yet dared deceive Heaven itself—never seeing that the state would fall and death draw near.

sentences.zh: 其罪八也。

translations.literal: This is his eighth crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is the eighth of his crimes.

sentences.zh: 設官分職，貴在銓衡；

translations.literal: Establishing offices and dividing duties values balance in selection;
translations.idiomatic: Setting offices and dividing duties depends on fair selection;

sentences.zh: 察獄問刑，無聞販鬻。

translations.literal: examining prisons and inquiring into punishments—never was buying and selling heard of.
translations.idiomatic: examining cases and judging punishments—never with justice sold for coin.

sentences.zh: 而錢神起論，銅臭為公，梁冀受黃金之蛇，孟佗薦蒲萄之酒。

translations.literal: Yet the god of money rose in discourse and the stink of copper became lord; Liang Ji received a golden snake, Meng Tuo presented grape wine.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the god of money ruled debate and the stink of copper became lord; Liang Ji took a golden snake, Meng Tuo offered grape wine for office.

sentences.zh: 遂使彝倫攸篸，政以賄成，君子在野，小人在位。

translations.literal: Thus constant norms were overthrown, government was achieved by bribes, gentlemen were in the wilds, and petty men held office.
translations.idiomatic: Constant norms collapsed, government was bought, gentlemen languished in the wilds, and petty men held office.

sentences.zh: 積薪居上，同汲黯之言；

translations.literal: Heaped firewood sat above—the same as Ji An's words;
translations.idiomatic: Heaped firewood sat above—just as Ji An warned;

sentences.zh: 囊錢不如，傷趙壹之賦。

translations.literal: purse money was not equal—grieving Zhao Yi's lament.
translations.idiomatic: purse money could not compare—grieving as in Zhao Yi's lament.

sentences.zh: 其罪九也。

translations.literal: This is his ninth crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is the ninth of his crimes.

sentences.zh: 宣尼有言，無信不立，用命賞祖，義豈食言？

translations.literal: Confucius said: without trust nothing stands; those who risk life are rewarded at the ancestral shrine—how in righteousness could words be eaten?
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said that without trust nothing stands, and those who risk their lives are rewarded at the shrine—how then break one's word in righteousness?

sentences.zh: 自昏主嗣位，每歲行幸，南北巡狩，東西征伐。

translations.literal: From the time the benighted ruler succeeded, each year he traveled on progress, touring north and south, campaigning east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Since the benighted ruler succeeded, every year he toured—north and south on progress, east and west on campaign.

sentences.zh: 至如浩亹陪蹕，東都守固，閿鄉野戰，雁門解圍。

translations.literal: Such as escorting at Haowan, holding firm the Eastern Capital, field battle at Wen Township, relieving siege at Yanmen—
translations.idiomatic: At Haowan he escorted the train, at the Eastern Capital he held the line, at Wen Township he fought in the field, at Yanmen he lifted a siege—

sentences.zh: 自外征夫，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: beyond these the campaigners cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: and beyond these the campaigns are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 既立功勳，須酬官爵。

translations.literal: Once merit is achieved, rank and title must be repaid.
translations.idiomatic: Once merit is won, rank and reward must follow.

sentences.zh: 而志懷翻覆，言行浮詭，危急則勳賞懸授，克定則絲綸不行，異商鞅之頒金，同項王之剚印。

translations.literal: Yet his intent was treacherous and his words and acts fickle—in crisis merit rewards were dangled, once victory was secured the edicts were not issued, unlike Shang Yang's distribution of gold, the same as Xiang Yu's grinding of seals.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his heart was treacherous and his words fickle—rewards were promised in crisis but withheld in victory, unlike Shang Yang's gold, like Xiang Yu grinding his seals.

sentences.zh: 芳餌之下，必有懸魚，惜其重賞，求人死力，走丸逆坡，匹此非難。

translations.literal: Beneath fragrant bait fish must hang; sparing heavy rewards yet seeking men's utmost effort—rolling a pellet uphill is not hard to match.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath fragrant bait the fish must hang; yet sparing rich reward while demanding men's lives—rolling a ball uphill is easier than this.

sentences.zh: 凡百驍雄，誰不仇怨。

translations.literal: Of all the fierce heroes, who did not harbor hatred?
translations.idiomatic: Which of the brave heroes did not nurse hatred?

sentences.zh: 至於匹夫蕞爾，宿諾不虧，既在乘輿，二三其德。

translations.literal: As for a mere commoner, tiny and slight, an old promise is not broken—yet once on the imperial carriage he is twice and thrice in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: A common man keeps an old promise unbroken—yet seated on the imperial carriage he is faithless twice and thrice over.

sentences.zh: 其罪十也。

translations.literal: This is his tenth crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is the tenth of his crimes.

sentences.zh: 有一於此，未或不亡。

translations.literal: With one of these, none fails to perish.
translations.idiomatic: With any one of these, what state could survive?

sentences.zh: 況四維不張，三靈總瘁，無小無大，愚夫愚婦，共識殷亡，咸知夏滅。

translations.literal: How much more when the four bonds are not spread and the three spirits are all afflicted—great and small alike, foolish men and foolish women all know Yin will fall and all know Xia is ended.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the four bonds are broken and the three spirits afflicted—high and low, men and women alike know Yin must fall and Xia is ended.

sentences.zh: 罄南山之竹，書罪未窮；

translations.literal: Exhaust the bamboo of South Mountain to write his crimes—they would not be exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Exhaust the bamboo of South Mountain and his crimes would still not be written out;

sentences.zh: 決東海之波，流惡難盡。

translations.literal: drain the waves of the eastern sea—his flowing evil could not be emptied.
translations.idiomatic: drain the eastern sea and his flowing evil would still not run dry.

sentences.zh: 是以窮奇災于上國，猰暴于中原。

translations.literal: Therefore Qiongqi brought disaster to the upper realm and Yayu ravaged the central plain.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Qiongqi brought disaster upon the realm and Yayu ravaged the central plain.

sentences.zh: 三河縱封豕之貪，四海被長蛇之毒，百姓殲亡，殆無遺類，十分為計，才一而已。

translations.literal: The Three Rivers let loose the greed of a penned boar; the four seas suffered the venom of a long serpent—the common people were slaughtered until almost none remained; of ten parts, only one remained.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Rivers unleashed a penned boar's greed; the four seas suffered a serpent's venom—the people were slaughtered until scarcely one in ten remained.

sentences.zh: 蒼生懍懍，咸憂杞國之崩；

translations.literal: The black-haired people were fearful, all worried over the collapse of the state of Qi;
translations.idiomatic: The people trembled, all fearing the fall of the state of Qi;

sentences.zh: 赤子嗷嗷，但愁曆陽之陷。

translations.literal: red infants wailed, grieving only the fall of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: infants wailed, grieving only the fall of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 且國祚將改，必有常期，六百殷亡之年，三十姬終之世。

translations.literal: Moreover the dynastic fortune is about to change—there must be a fixed term: six hundred years when Yin perished, thirty generations when Ji ended.
translations.idiomatic: The dynastic fortune is about to turn, and there is a fixed term—six hundred years for Yin, thirty generations for Zhou.

sentences.zh: 故讖籙云隋氏三十六年而滅，此則厭德之象已彰，代終之兆先見。

translations.literal: Thus prophecies say the house of Sui will perish in thirty-six years—here the sign of exhausted virtue is already clear, the omen of a dynasty's end is seen in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Prophecies say the Sui will fall in thirty-six years—the sign of exhausted virtue is clear and the dynasty's end is foreseen.

sentences.zh: 皇天無親，惟德是輔。

translations.literal: August Heaven is not partial—it assists only virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is impartial and assists only virtue.

sentences.zh: 況乃攙搶竟天，申繻謂之除舊；

translations.literal: Moreover comets fill the sky—Shen Xu called this removal of the old;
translations.idiomatic: Comets fill the sky—Shen Xu called this the clearing away of the old;

sentences.zh: 歲星入井，甘公以為義興。

translations.literal: the Year Star entered the Well—Gan Gong took it as righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: the Year Star entered the Well—Gan Gong read it as the rise of righteous rule.

sentences.zh: 兼朱雀門燒，正陽日蝕，狐鳴鬼哭，川竭山崩。

translations.literal: Together with the Vermilion Bird Gate burning, an eclipse on the first yang day, foxes crying and ghosts weeping, streams drying and mountains collapsing.
translations.idiomatic: The Vermilion Bird Gate burned, the sun was eclipsed on the first yang day, foxes cried and ghosts wailed, streams dried up and mountains collapsed.

sentences.zh: 並是宗廟為墟之妖，荊棘旅庭之事。

translations.literal: All are omens of ancestral temples turned to ruins, of thorns and brambles lodging in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: All are omens of temples in ruins and thorns lodging in the royal courtyard.

sentences.zh: 夏氏則災釁非多，殷人則咎征更少。

translations.literal: The house of Xia had no more disasters and portents; the people of Yin had even fewer signs of blame.
translations.idiomatic: Xia had fewer disasters than this; Yin had fewer omens of blame.

sentences.zh: 牽牛入漢，方知大亂之期；

translations.literal: When the Ox Leader entered the Han River, then one knew the season of great disorder;
translations.idiomatic: When the Ox Leader entered the Han River, the season of great disorder was known;

sentences.zh: 王良策馬，始驗兵車之會。

translations.literal: when Wang Liang drove his horses, the convergence of war chariots was first verified.
translations.idiomatic: when Wang Liang drove his horses, the gathering of war chariots was confirmed.

sentences.zh: 今者順人將革，先天不違，大誓孟津，陳命景亳，三千列國，八百諸侯，不謀而同辭，不召而自至。

translations.literal: Now as the people's will is about to change, Heaven's timing is not opposed—the great oath at Meng Ford, the mandate proclaimed at Jing Bo; three thousand states, eight hundred lords, without counsel speaking as one, without summons coming of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Now as the people's will turns and Heaven's timing is at hand—the great oath at Meng Ford, the mandate at Jing Bo—three thousand states and eight hundred lords speak as one without counsel and come without summons.

sentences.zh: 轟轟隱隱，如霆如雷，彪虎嘯而穀風生，應龍驤而景雲起。

translations.literal: Booming and rumbling like thunder and lightning; striped tigers roar and valley winds rise, responding dragons prance and auspicious clouds ascend.
translations.idiomatic: The host thunders like storm and lightning; tigers roar and valley winds rise, dragons prance and auspicious clouds ascend.

sentences.zh: 我魏公聰明神武，齊聖廣淵，總七德而在躬，包九功而挺出。

translations.literal: Our Duke of Wei is wise and divinely martial, equal to the sage and broad and deep, gathering the seven virtues in his person and encompassing the nine achievements as he stands forth.
translations.idiomatic: Our Duke of Wei is wise and martial, sage-like and far-reaching, embodying the seven virtues and encompassing the nine achievements.

sentences.zh: 周太保、魏公之孫，上柱國、蒲山公之子。

translations.literal: Grandson of the Zhou Grand Tutor and Duke of Wei, son of the Superior Pillar of State and Duke of Pushan.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson of the Zhou Grand Tutor and Duke of Wei, son of the Superior Pillar of State and Duke of Pushan.

sentences.zh: 家傳盛德，武王承季曆之基；

translations.literal: His house transmits flourishing virtue; King Wu received the foundation of Jili's line;
translations.idiomatic: His house transmits great virtue, as King Wu received Jili's foundation;

sentences.zh: 地啟元勳，世祖嗣元皇之業。

translations.literal: the land opened to founding merit, and the founding emperor succeeded the primal emperor's enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: the land opened to founding merit, and the founding emperor succeeded the primal emperor's enterprise.

sentences.zh: 篤生白水，日角之相便彰；

translations.literal: Born firmly at Baishui, the sun-horn physiognomy was at once revealed;
translations.idiomatic: Born at Baishui, the sun-horn mark of emperors was revealed;

sentences.zh: 載誕丹陵，大寶之文斯著。

translations.literal: borne at Danling, the text of the great treasure was then displayed.
translations.idiomatic: born at Danling, the script of the great mandate was displayed.

sentences.zh: 加以姓符圖緯，名協歌謠，六合所以歸心，三靈所以改卜。

translations.literal: Added to this, his surname matched charts and wefts, his name accorded with songs and ballads—within the six directions hearts therefore turned to him, and the three spirits therefore changed their divination.
translations.idiomatic: His surname matched the charts, his name the songs—the six directions turned their hearts and the three spirits changed their omens.

sentences.zh: 文王厄於羑里，赤雀方來；

translations.literal: King Wen was confined at Youli and the red sparrow had just come;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen was confined at Youli when the red sparrow came;

sentences.zh: 高祖隱于碭山，彤雲自起。

translations.literal: the High Ancestor hid at Dang Mountain and cinnabar clouds rose of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: the High Ancestor hid at Dang Mountain and cinnabar clouds rose of themselves.

sentences.zh: 兵誅不道，《赤伏》至自長安；

translations.literal: With arms he punished the unrighteous and the Red Fu arrived from Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: He took up arms against the unrighteous and the Red Fu prophecy came from Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 鋒銳難當，黃星出於梁、宋。

translations.literal: his sharp edge was hard to withstand and the yellow star appeared in Liang and Song.
translations.idiomatic: his edge was irresistible and the yellow star appeared over Liang and Song.

sentences.zh: 九五龍飛之始，天人豹變之初，曆試諸難，大敵彌勇。

translations.literal: At the beginning when the nine-five dragon flies, at the first hour when Heaven and man transform like leopards—tested through many hardships, against great foes he grew ever braver.
translations.idiomatic: At the hour when the dragon takes flight, when Heaven and man transform—tested through hardships, he grew braver against greater foes.

sentences.zh: 上柱國、司徒、東郡公翟讓功宣締構，翼亮經綸，伊尹之佐成湯，蕭何之輔高帝。

translations.literal: Superior Pillar of State, Minister of Education, Duke of Dong Commandery Zhai Rang—his merit proclaimed in founding and construction, his wings brightening statecraft—Yi Yin's assistance to Cheng Tang, Xiao He's support of the High Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Superior Pillar Zhai Rang, Duke of Dong—his merit in founding the enterprise, his counsel in statecraft—like Yi Yin to Cheng Tang, like Xiao He to the High Emperor.

sentences.zh: 上柱國、總管、齊國公孟讓，柱國、曆城公孟暢，柱國、絳郡公裴行儼，大將軍、左長史邴元真等，並運籌千里，勇冠三軍，擊劍則截蛟斷鰲，彎弧則吟猿落雁。

translations.literal: Superior Pillar, Director-General, Duke of Qi Meng Rang; Pillar of State, Duke of Licheng Meng Chang; Pillar of State, Duke of Jiang Commandery Pei Xingyan; Great General, Left Chief Clerk Bing Yuanzhen and others—all schemed for a thousand li, courage crowning the three armies; with sword-stroke they severed flood dragon and giant turtle; bending the bow they made crying apes fall and wild geese drop.
translations.idiomatic: Superior Pillar Meng Rang of Qi, Pillar Meng Chang of Licheng, Pillar Pei Xingyan of Jiang, Great General Bing Yuanzhen and others—all schemed across a thousand li and led the armies in courage; with sword they could sever dragon and turtle, with bow bring down ape and goose.

sentences.zh: 韓、彭、絳、灌，成沛公之基；

translations.literal: Han, Peng, Jiang, and Guan laid the foundation for the Duke of Pei;
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin, Peng Yue, Zhou Bo, and Guan Ying laid the Duke of Pei's foundation;

sentences.zh: 寇、賈、吳、馮，奉蕭王之業。

translations.literal: Kou, Jia, Wu, and Feng upheld the enterprise of the King of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Xun, Jia Fu, Wu Han, and Feng Yi upheld the King of Xiao's enterprise.

sentences.zh: 復有蒙輪挾輈之士，拔距投石之夫，驥馬追風，吳戈照日。
