translations.literal: Again there were men who took the wheel hub under their arms, champions of leaping and stone-casting, thoroughbred horses chasing the wind, Wu halberds gleaming in the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Again there were men who seized chariot hubs in battle, champions of leaping and stone-throwing, horses swift as wind, Wu halberds flashing in the sun.

sentences.zh: 魏公屬當期運，伏茲億兆。

translations.literal: The Duke of Wei meets the season's fortune and bows before these hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Wei meets the season's fortune and bows before the hundred millions.

sentences.zh: 躬擐甲胄，跋涉山川，櫛風沐雨，豈辭勞倦，遂起西伯之師，將問南巢之罪。

translations.literal: He personally donned armor, trudged mountains and rivers, combed the wind and bathed in rain—how would he decline weariness? Thus he raised the army of the Western Earl to bring the crime of Nan Chao to account.
translations.idiomatic: He donned armor himself, crossed mountains and rivers, weathered wind and rain without complaint, and raised the army of the Western Earl to punish the crimes of Nan Chao.

sentences.zh: 百萬成旅，四七為名，呼吸則河、渭絕流，叱吒則嵩、華自拔。

translations.literal: A million formed into hosts, four times seven in name; at a breath the Yellow and Wei rivers ceased flowing, at a shout Song and Hua mountains uprooted themselves.
translations.idiomatic: A million men formed into hosts; at a breath the Yellow and Wei rivers would cease, at a shout Song and Hua would tremble.

sentences.zh: 以此攻城，何城不陷；

translations.literal: With this to assault cities, what city would not fall;
translations.idiomatic: With such force to assault cities, what city would not fall;

sentences.zh: 以此擊陣，何陣不摧！

translations.literal: with this to strike formations, what formation would not be shattered!
translations.idiomatic: with such force to strike formations, what formation would not shatter!

sentences.zh: 譬猶瀉滄海而灌殘熒，舉昆侖而壓小卵。

translations.literal: It is like pouring the blue sea to irrigate a dying flame, or lifting Kunlun to crush a tiny egg.
translations.idiomatic: It is like pouring the sea to douse a dying flame, or lifting Kunlun to crush a tiny egg.

sentences.zh: 鼓行而進，百道俱前，以今月二十一日屆於東都。

translations.literal: Beating drums they advance; a hundred routes press forward together—on the twenty-first day of this month they will arrive at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Beating drums they advance on a hundred routes—the twenty-first of this month they will reach the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 而昏朝文武、留守段達等，昆吾惡稔，飛廉奸佞，久迷天數，敢拒義兵，驅率醜徒，眾有十萬，回洛倉北，遂來舉斧。

translations.literal: Yet the benighted court's civil and military officials, the left-behind Duan Da and others—Kunwu's evil ripe, Feilian's treachery and flattery—long deluded by Heaven's count, dare resist the righteous army, driving ugly followers, a host of a hundred thousand north of the Huiluo granary, and thus come to raise the axe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the benighted court's officials, the garrison commander Duan Da and others—evil ripe as Kunwu, treacherous as Feilian—long blind to Heaven's will, dare resist the righteous army and lead a hundred thousand rabble north of Huiluo granary to raise the axe against us.

sentences.zh: 於是熊羆角逐，貔虎爭先，因其倒戈之心，乘我破竹之勢，曾未旋踵，瓦解冰銷，坑卒則長平未多，積甲則熊耳為小。

translations.literal: Thereupon bears and brown bears strove, pixiu and tigers vied to lead; seizing their hearts to turn their spears, riding our bamboo-splitting momentum—before they could turn the heel they melted like ice; buried soldiers were not as many as at Changping, heaped armor made Xiong'er seem small.
translations.idiomatic: Bears and tigers vied in the charge; seizing their will to turn their spears and riding our irresistible momentum, the enemy melted like ice before they could turn—fewer dead than at Changping, less armor heaped than at Xiong'er.

sentences.zh: 達等助桀為虐，嬰城自固，梯沖亂舞，徒設九拒之謀；

translations.literal: Da and the rest aided Jie in tyranny, clung to the city to hold firm, scaling ladders and rams danced wildly—they vainly set the plan of nine refusals;
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da and the rest aided tyranny like Jie's minions, clung to the walls, and vainly deployed ladders and rams with their ninefold defenses;

sentences.zh: 鼓角將鳴，空憑百樓之險。

translations.literal: drums and horns were about to sound—they relied in vain on the peril of a hundred towers.
translations.idiomatic: drums and horns were about to sound—they relied in vain on their hundred towers.

sentences.zh: 燕巢衛幕，魚游宋池，殄滅之期，匪朝伊暮。

translations.literal: Swallows nest on Wei curtains, fish swim in Song pools—the day of extermination is not morning but evening.
translations.idiomatic: Swallows nest on curtains, fish swim in pools—the day of their destruction is not far off.

sentences.zh: 然興洛、虎牢，國家儲積，我已先據，為日久矣。

translations.literal: Yet Xingluo and Hulao—the state's stored grain—we have already seized first, and for long.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xingluo and Hulao, the state's granaries, we have held for a long time already.

sentences.zh: 既得回洛，又取黎陽，天下之倉，盡非隋有。

translations.literal: Having gained Huiluo, we also took Liyang—the granaries of the realm are no longer Sui's.
translations.idiomatic: Having taken Huiluo, we also seized Liyang—the empire's granaries are no longer the Sui's.

sentences.zh: 四方起義，足食足兵，無前無敵。

translations.literal: Uprisings on four sides—food enough, troops enough, without peer and without foe.
translations.idiomatic: Uprisings on every side—food and troops in abundance, without peer and without rival.

sentences.zh: 裴光祿仁基，雄才上將，受脤專征，遐邇攸憑，安危是托，乃識機知變，遷殷事夏。

translations.literal: Pei Renji, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, a heroic general and superior commander, received the sacrificial meat and held independent campaign—near and far relied on him, safety and danger were entrusted to him—yet he knew the moment and understood change, shifting from Yin to serve Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Renji, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, a heroic commander entrusted with independent campaign—near and far relied on him for safety—yet read the moment and shifted allegiance from Yin to Xia.

sentences.zh: 袁謙擒自藍水，張須陀獲在滎陽，竇慶戰沒于淮南，郭詢授首于河北，隋之亡候，聊可知也。

translations.literal: Yuan Qian was captured from Lanshui, Zhang Xutuo taken at Xingyang, Dou Qing fell in battle at Huainan, Guo Xun surrendered his head in Hebei—the signs of Sui's fall can roughly be known.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qian was captured at Lanshui, Zhang Xutuo taken at Xingyang, Dou Qing killed at Huainan, Guo Xun beheaded in Hebei—the signs of Sui's fall are plain to see.

sentences.zh: 清河公房彥藻，近秉戎律，略地東南，師之所臨，風行電擊。

translations.literal: Fang Yanzao, Duke of Qinghe, recently held military law and seized lands in the southeast—wherever his army arrived, wind ran and lightning struck.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yanzao, Duke of Qinghe, recently took command in the southeast—wherever his army went, it struck like wind and lightning.

sentences.zh: 安陸、汝南，隨機蕩定；

translations.literal: Anlu and Runan were pacified as opportunity allowed;
translations.idiomatic: Anlu and Runan were pacified as opportunity allowed;

sentences.zh: 淮安、濟陽，俄然送款。

translations.literal: Huai'an and Jiyang soon offered submission.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'an and Jiyang soon submitted.

sentences.zh: 徐圓朗已平魯郡，孟海公又破濟陽，海內英雄，咸來回應。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanlang has already pacified Lu Commandery, Meng Haigong has again broken Jiyang—heroes within the seas all come in response.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang has pacified Lu, Meng Haigong has taken Jiyang—heroes across the land rally in response.

sentences.zh: 封民贍取平原之境，郝孝德據黎陽之倉，李士雄虎視于長平，王德仁鷹揚於上黨。

translations.literal: Feng Min took the lands of Pingyuan; Hao Xiaode held the granary of Liyang; Li Shixiong glared like a tiger at Changping; Wang Deren soared like an eagle at Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Min seized Pingyuan, Hao Xiaode held Liyang's granary, Li Shixiong glared from Changping, and Wang Deren soared from Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 滑公李景、考功郎中房山基發自臨渝，劉興祖起于白朔，崔白駒在潁川起，方獻伯以譙郡來，各擁數萬之兵，俱期牧野之會。

translations.literal: Li Jing, Duke of Hua, and Fang Shanji, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel, set out from Linyu; Liu Xingzu rose at Baishuo; Cui Baiju rose in Yingchuan; Fang Xianbo came with Qiao Commandery—each commanding tens of thousands of troops, all expecting the meeting at Muye.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing of Hua and Personnel Bureau Director Fang Shanji marched from Linyu; Liu Xingzu rose at Baishuo; Cui Baiju in Yingchuan; Fang Xianbo from Qiao—each with tens of thousands, all bound for Muye.

sentences.zh: 滄溟之右，函谷以東，牛酒獻於軍前，壺漿盈于道路。

translations.literal: To the right of the blue sea, east of Hangu Pass, oxen and wine were offered before the army and pots of broth filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: East of the passes and west of the sea, oxen and wine were offered before the army and pots of broth lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 諸君等並衣冠世胄，杞梓良才，神鼎靈繹之秋，裂地封侯之始，豹變鵲起，今也其時，鼉鳴鱉應，見機而作，宜各鳩率子弟，共建功名。

translations.literal: You gentlemen are all heirs of cap and gown, fine timber and good talent—in the autumn when the divine cauldron's spirit runs clear, at the beginning when lands are split and marquisates enfeoffed, leopards transform and magpies rise—now is the hour; when the alligator calls the turtle answers. Seeing the moment, act—each of you should gather your sons and younger brothers and together build merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: You are all heirs of noble houses and fine talent—in the hour when the divine mandate shifts and fiefs are granted, the moment for bold transformation has come. Read the signs and act: gather your kin and build merit together.

sentences.zh: 耿弇之赴光武，蕭何之奉高帝，豈止金章紫綬，華蓋朱輪，富貴以重當年，忠貞以傳奕葉，豈不盛哉！

translations.literal: Geng Yan going to Guangwu, Xiao He serving the High Emperor—was it only golden seals and purple cords, flowered canopies and vermilion wheels? Wealth and honor to weight the present year, loyalty and constancy to pass through generations of leaves—how is it not grand!
translations.idiomatic: Like Geng Yan rallying to Guangwu or Xiao He serving the High Emperor—not only golden seals and purple cords, flowered canopies and vermilion wheels, but wealth to dignify the present and loyalty to pass through generations—how grand!

sentences.zh: 若隋代官人，同吠堯之犬，尚荷王莽之恩，仍懷蒯聵之祿。

translations.literal: If Sui officials are like dogs that bark at Yao, still bearing Wang Mang's favor, still cherishing the salary of Kuai Kui—
translations.idiomatic: If any Sui officials are like dogs that bark at Yao, still grateful to Wang Mang, still clinging to Kuai Kui's salary—

sentences.zh: 審配死于袁氏，不如張郃歸曹；

translations.literal: Shen Pei died for the Yuan clan—better to be Zhang He returning to Cao;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei died for the Yuans—better to be Zhang He going over to Cao;

sentences.zh: 范增困于項王，未若陳平從漢。

translations.literal: Fan Zeng was trapped under King Xiang—not equal to Chen Ping following Han.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zeng was trapped with Xiang Yu—not as wise as Chen Ping joining Han.

sentences.zh: 魏公推以赤心，當加好爵，擇木而處，令不自疑。

translations.literal: The Duke of Wei extends his red heart—you should receive fine rank; choose your tree and settle, and need not doubt yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Wei offers his sincere heart and will grant fine rank; choose your tree and settle without doubt.

sentences.zh: 脫猛虎猶豫，舟中敵國，夙沙之人共縛其主，彭寵之僕自殺其君，高官上賞，即以相授。

translations.literal: If you leave the fierce tiger hesitating, an enemy state is in the boat—the men of Susha together bound their lord, Peng Chong's servant himself killed his ruler; high office and supreme reward will be granted at once.
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate like a tiger in doubt, you make an enemy within the boat—remember how the men of Susha bound their lord and Peng Chong's servant killed his master; high office and rich reward await at once.

sentences.zh: 如暗於成事，守迷不反，昆山縱火，玉石俱焚，爾等噬臍，悔將何及！

translations.literal: If blind to success and clinging to delusion without return, when Kun Mountain sets the fire jade and stone burn together—you will bite your navels; what regret will reach you then!
translations.idiomatic: If you are blind to success and cling to error, when Kun Mountain burns jade and stone perish together—you will bite your navels in regret when it is too late!

sentences.zh: 黃河帶地，明餘旦旦之言；

translations.literal: The Yellow River girdles the land—making clear these words spoken at dawn;
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River girdles the land—witness these words sworn at dawn;

sentences.zh: 皎日麗天，知我勤勤之意。

translations.literal: the bright sun beautifies the sky—know my earnest and diligent intent.
translations.idiomatic: the bright sun fills the sky—know my earnest intent.

sentences.zh: 佈告海內，咸使聞知。

translations.literal: Proclaim throughout the seas and make all hear and know.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed throughout the realm so all may hear.

sentences.zh: 祖君彥之辭也。

translations.literal: This was the composition of Zu Junyan.
translations.idiomatic: This proclamation was written by Zu Junyan.

sentences.zh: 俄而德韜、德方俱死，復以鄭頲為左司馬，鄭虔象為右司馬。

translations.literal: Soon Detao and Defang both died; he again appointed Zheng Ting as Left Major and Zheng Qianxiang as Right Major.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Detao and Defang both died; Mi appointed Zheng Ting as Left Major and Zheng Qianxiang as Right Major.

sentences.zh: 柴孝和說密曰：「秦地阻山帶河，西楚背之而亡，漢高都之而霸。

translations.literal: Chai Xiaohe urged Mi: "The Qin lands are blocked by mountains and girdled by rivers; Western Chu turned its back on them and perished, while Han Gaozu made them his capital and became hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Xiaohe urged Mi, "The Qin lands are walled by mountains and rivers; Western Chu turned its back on them and perished, while Han Gaozu made them his capital and rose to supremacy.

sentences.zh: 如愚意者，令仁基守回洛，翟讓守洛口，明公親簡精銳，西襲長安，百姓孰不郊迎，必當有征無戰。

translations.literal: In my humble view, have Renji guard Huiluo, Zhai Rang guard Luokou, and my lord personally select elite troops to strike west at Chang'an—which of the common people would not greet you in the suburbs? You will surely have campaign without battle.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, let Renji hold Huiluo, Zhai Rang hold Luokou, and you personally lead picked troops west against Chang'an—the people will greet you in the suburbs, and you will conquer without fighting.

sentences.zh: 既克京邑，業固兵強，方更長驅崤函，掃蕩東洛，傳檄指捴，天下可定。

translations.literal: Once the capital is taken, your enterprise will be firm and your troops strong; then drive further through Xiaohan Pass, sweep the Eastern Capital, send proclamations to direct the host—the realm can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Once the capital is taken, your foundation will be firm and your army strong; then march through Xiaohan, sweep the Eastern Capital, and send proclamations across the land—the realm will be settled.

sentences.zh: 但今英雄競起，實恐他人我先，一朝失之，噬臍何及！

translations.literal: But now heroes rise in rivalry—I truly fear another will act before me; lose it in a morning and what regret can reach you!
translations.idiomatic: But heroes are rising everywhere, and I fear another may act first—lose the moment and regret will come too late!

sentences.zh: 」密曰：「君之所圖，僕亦思之久矣，誠乃上策。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "What you plan, I too have pondered long—it is truly the upper strategy.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi said, "Your plan is one I have considered for a long time—it is truly the best strategy.

sentences.zh: 但昏主尚存，從兵猶眾，我之所部，並是山東人，既見未下洛陽，何肯相隨西入？

translations.literal: But the benighted ruler still exists and his following troops are still many; those under my command are all men of Shandong—seeing that Luoyang is not yet taken, how would they agree to follow west?
translations.idiomatic: But the benighted emperor still lives and his troops are many; my men are all from Shandong—seeing Luoyang still untaken, who would follow me west?

sentences.zh: 諸將出於群盜，留之各競雄雌。

translations.literal: The generals came from bandit bands; left behind, each would vie for dominance.
translations.idiomatic: The generals came from bandit bands; left behind, each would vie for supremacy.

sentences.zh: 若然者，殆將敗矣！

translations.literal: If so, we would likely be defeated!
translations.idiomatic: If we did that, we would likely be ruined!

sentences.zh: 」密將兵鋒甚銳，每入苑與隋軍連戰。

translations.literal: " Mi's army edge was very sharp; each time he entered the park he fought in succession with Sui troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi's troops fought fiercely, battling Sui forces again and again in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 會密為流矢所中，臥于營內，東都復出兵乘之，密眾大潰，棄回洛倉，歸於洛口。

translations.literal: It happened that Mi was struck by a stray arrow and lay in camp; the Eastern Capital again sent troops to strike while he was exposed—Mi's host collapsed utterly, abandoned the Huiluo granary, and returned to Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was struck by a stray arrow and confined to camp; the Eastern Capital sent troops to strike at his weakness—his army collapsed, abandoned Huiluo granary, and retreated to Luokou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣王世充率勁卒五萬擊之，密與戰，不利，孝和溺死于洛水，密哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang sent Wang Shichong with fifty thousand crack troops to attack; Mi fought him without success. Xiaohe drowned in the Luo River and Mi wept for him in deepest grief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent Wang Shichong with fifty thousand elite troops; Mi fought him without success. Xiaohe drowned in the Luo River, and Mi wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 世充營於洛西，與密相拒百餘日，大小六十餘戰。

translations.literal: Shichong camped west of the Luo and faced Mi for more than a hundred days, fighting more than sixty battles great and small.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong camped west of the Luo and faced Mi for over a hundred days in more than sixty battles.

sentences.zh: 武陽郡丞元寶藏、黎陽賊帥李文柏、洹水賊帥張升、清河賊帥趙君德、平原賊帥郝孝德，並歸於密，共襲破黎陽倉，據之。

translations.literal: Yuan Baocang, assistant magistrate of Wuyang; Li Wenbai, bandit chief of Liyang; Zhang Sheng, bandit chief of Huanshui; Zhao Junde, bandit chief of Qinghe; Hao Xiaode, bandit chief of Pingyuan—all submitted to Mi and together raided and took the Liyang granary, holding it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Baocang of Wuyang, bandit leaders Li Wenbai, Zhang Sheng, Zhao Junde, and Hao Xiaode all joined Mi and together seized the Liyang granary.

sentences.zh: 永安大族周法明舉江、黃之地以附密，齊郡賊帥徐圓朗、任城大俠徐師仁、淮陽太守趙佗皆歸之。

translations.literal: Zhou Faming, a great clan of Yong'an, raised the lands of the Yang and Huang to attach to Mi; Xu Yuanlang, bandit chief of Qi Commandery; Xu Shiren, great knight of Rencheng; Zhao Tuo, prefect of Huaiyang—all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Faming of Yong'an brought the Yang and Huang regions to Mi; Xu Yuanlang, Xu Shiren, and Prefect Zhao Tuo of Huaiyang all submitted.

sentences.zh: 翟讓部將王儒信勸讓為大塚宰，總統眾務，以奪密之權。

translations.literal: Zhai Rang's officer Wang Ruxin urged Rang to become Grand Minister of Works and oversee all affairs, to seize Mi's power.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ruxin, an officer of Zhai Rang, urged Rang to become Grand Minister of Works and take control of all affairs, seizing power from Mi.

sentences.zh: 讓兄寬復謂讓曰：「天子止可自作，安得與人！

translations.literal: Rang's elder brother Kuan again said to Rang: "The Son of Heaven can only be made by oneself—how can one share it with others!
translations.idiomatic: Rang's elder brother Kuan told him again, "An emperor makes himself—how can you share the throne with another!

sentences.zh: 汝若不能作，我當為之。

translations.literal: If you cannot do it, I shall.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot do it, I will.

sentences.zh: 」密聞其言，陰有圖讓之計。

translations.literal: " Mi heard these words and secretly formed a plan against Rang.
translations.idiomatic: " Hearing this, Mi secretly plotted against Rang.

sentences.zh: 會世充列陣而至，讓出拒之，為世充所擊，讓軍少失利，密與單雄信等率精銳赴之，世充敗走。

translations.literal: It happened that Shichong drew up ranks and came; Rang went out to resist, was struck by Shichong, and Rang's army suffered a slight setback. Mi with Shan Xiongxin and others led elite troops to the rescue and Shichong fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong advanced in battle order, Rang went out to meet him and suffered a setback; Mi rushed up with Shan Xiongxin and elite troops, and Shichong was driven off.

sentences.zh: 明日，讓徑至密所，欲為宴樂，密具饌以待之，其所將左右，各分令就食。

translations.literal: The next day Rang came straight to Mi's quarters wishing to feast and make merry; Mi prepared food to await him and had those Rang brought with him each separately ordered to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Rang came straight to Mi's camp for a feast; Mi prepared a meal and had Rang's attendants eat separately.

sentences.zh: 密引讓入坐，以良弓示讓，讓方引滿，密遣壯士自後斬之，並殺其兄寬及王儒信。

translations.literal: Mi led Rang in to sit, showed him a fine bow; as Rang was drawing it full Mi sent braves from behind to cut him down, and also killed his brother Kuan and Wang Ruxin.
translations.idiomatic: Mi seated Rang and showed him a fine bow; as Rang drew it to the full, Mi's men struck from behind and killed him, along with his brother Kuan and Wang Ruxin.

sentences.zh: 讓部將徐世勣為亂兵所斫，中重瘡，密遽止之，得免，單雄信等頓首求哀，密並釋而慰諭之。

translations.literal: Rang's officer Xu Shiji was hacked by disorderly troops and suffered grave wounds; Mi hastily stopped it and he was spared. Shan Xiongxin and others knocked their heads begging mercy; Mi released and comforted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiji was wounded in the confusion by grave cuts; Mi stopped the attack and spared him. Shan Xiongxin and others begged for mercy on their knees, and Mi released and reassured them.

sentences.zh: 於是詣讓連營，諭其將士，無敢動者。

translations.literal: He then went to Rang's linked camps and instructed the officers and soldiers—none dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Rang's camps and addressed the troops—none dared move.

sentences.zh: 乃命徐世勣、單雄信、王伯當分統其眾。

translations.literal: He then ordered Xu Shiji, Shan Xiongxin, and Wang Bodang to command Rang's followers separately.
translations.idiomatic: He put Xu Shiji, Shan Xiongxin, and Wang Bodang in command of Rang's former followers.

sentences.zh: 未幾，世充襲倉城，密復破之。

translations.literal: Before long Shichong raided the granary city and Mi again defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shichong raided the granary city, and Mi defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 世充復移營洛北，造浮橋，悉眾以擊密，密與千餘騎拒之，不利而退。

translations.literal: Shichong again moved camp north of the Luo, built a pontoon bridge, and led his entire force against Mi; Mi with more than a thousand cavalry resisted but without success and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong moved camp north of the Luo, built a pontoon bridge, and attacked with his full force; Mi met him with a thousand cavalry, failed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 世充因薄其城下，密簡銳卒數百人以邀之，世充大潰，爭趣浮橋，溺死者數萬。

translations.literal: Shichong therefore pressed close beneath the walls; Mi selected several hundred elite soldiers to intercept him—Shichong collapsed utterly, all rushing for the pontoon bridge, and tens of thousands drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong pressed close under the walls; Mi sent several hundred picked men against him—Shichong's army collapsed, rushed the pontoon bridge, and tens of thousands drowned.

sentences.zh: 虎賁郎將楊威、王辯、霍舉、劉長恭、梁德、董智皆沒於陣，世充僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Tiger Guard Generals Yang Wei, Wang Bian, Huo Ju, Liu Changgong, Liang De, and Dong Zhi all perished in the battle; Shichong barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger Guard Generals Yang Wei, Wang Bian, Huo Ju, Liu Changgong, Liang De, and Dong Zhi all died in battle; Shichong barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 其夜，大雨雪，士卒凍死者殆盡。

translations.literal: That night heavy rain and snow fell; the soldiers who froze to death were nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: That night a heavy snowstorm fell, and nearly all his soldiers froze to death.

sentences.zh: 密乘勝陷偃師，於是修金墉城居之，有眾三十餘萬。

translations.literal: Mi followed victory to take Yanshi; he then repaired the Jinyong city wall to dwell there, with a following of more than three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Mi pressed the victory to take Yanshi, repaired Jinyong city as his seat, and commanded more than three hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 留守韋津又與密戰於上春門，津大敗，執於陣。

translations.literal: The left-behind Wei Jin again fought Mi at Shangchun Gate; Jin was utterly defeated and seized on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Wei Jin fought Mi again at Shangchun Gate, was routed, and captured in battle.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠宇文愷叛東都，降於密。

translations.literal: Director of Palace Construction Yuwen Kai rebelled from the Eastern Capital and surrendered to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Palace Construction Yuwen Kai defected from the Eastern Capital and surrendered to Mi.

sentences.zh: 東至海、岱，南至江、淮郡縣，莫不遣使歸密。

translations.literal: East to the sea and Dai, south to the Yang and Huai—commanderies and counties all sent envoys to submit to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: From the eastern sea to Dai in the east and the Yang and Huai in the south, commanderies and counties sent envoys to submit to Mi.

sentences.zh: 竇建德、朱粲、楊士林、孟海公、徐圓朗、盧祖尚、周法明等並隨使通表於密勸進，於是密下官屬咸勸密即尊號，密曰：「東都未平，不可議此。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande, Zhu Can, Yang Shilin, Meng Haigong, Xu Yuanlang, Lu Zushang, Zhou Faming, and others all sent envoys with memorials urging Mi to advance to the imperial title; thereupon all Mi's subordinate officials urged him to assume the exalted designation. Mi said: "The Eastern Capital is not yet pacified—we cannot discuss this.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande, Zhu Can, Yang Shilin, Meng Haigong, Xu Yuanlang, Lu Zushang, Zhou Faming, and others sent memorials urging him to take the throne; his officials all pressed him to assume the imperial title. Mi said, "The Eastern Capital is not yet pacified—we cannot discuss this yet.

sentences.zh: 及義旗建，密負其強盛，欲自為盟主，乃致書呼高祖為兄，請合從以滅隋，大略云欲與高祖為盟津之會，殪商辛於牧野，執子嬰於咸陽，其旨以弑後主執代王為意。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, Mi relied on his strength and wished to be alliance leader himself; he sent a letter calling the High Ancestor "elder brother," requesting joint action to destroy Sui. In outline it said he wished with the High Ancestor to meet at Meng Ford, slay Shang Xin at Muye, and seize Ziying at Xianyang—the intent being to kill the late ruler and seize the Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous banner was raised, Mi, confident in his strength, wished to be alliance leader himself; he wrote calling the High Ancestor "elder brother" and proposed a joint campaign to destroy the Sui—meeting at Meng Ford, destroying the tyrant at Muye, and seizing the puppet emperor at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽書笑曰：「李密陸梁放肆，不可以折簡致之。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor read the letter and laughed: "Li Mi is insolent and unrestrained—we cannot summon him with a brief note.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor read the letter and laughed, "Li Mi is insolent and unrestrained—not someone to summon with a brief note.

sentences.zh: 吾方安輯京師，未遑東討，即相阻絕，便是更生一秦。

translations.literal: I am just now settling the capital and have no leisure for an eastern campaign; if we block each other at once, it is simply giving birth to another Qin.
translations.idiomatic: I am still settling the capital and have no time for an eastern campaign; if we block each other now, we simply create another Qin.

sentences.zh: 密今適所以為吾拒東都之兵，守成皋之扼，更求韓、彭，莫如用密。

translations.literal: Mi now happens to be blocking the Eastern Capital's troops for us and holding the choke point at Chenggao—seeking Han Xin and Peng Yue, none is better than using Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Mi now happens to be holding off the Eastern Capital's troops and guarding the Chenggao choke point—for Han Xin and Peng Yue, none serves better than Mi.

sentences.zh: 宜卑辭推獎，以驕其志，使其不虞於我。

translations.literal: We should use humble words and praise to swell his ambition, so he does not beware of us.
translations.idiomatic: We should use humble praise to swell his ambition so he does not beware of us.

sentences.zh: 我得入關，據蒲津而屯永豐，阻崤函而臨伊、洛，吾大事濟矣。

translations.literal: When I can enter the passes, hold Pujin and camp at Yongfeng, block Xiaohan and face the Yi and Luo—my great affair is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: When I enter the passes, hold Pujin, camp at Yongfeng, block Xiaohan, and face the Yi and Luo—my great enterprise will succeed.

sentences.zh: 」令記室溫大雅作書報密曰：

translations.literal: " He ordered Recorder Wen Daya to compose a reply to Mi, saying:
translations.idiomatic: " He had Recorder Wen Daya draft a reply to Mi:

sentences.zh: 「頃者，昆山火烈，海水群飛，赤縣丘墟，黔黎塗炭。

translations.literal: " Recently Kun Mountain's fire blazed fierce and the sea's waters flew in hosts; the red land became ruins and the black-haired people were smeared with charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: " Recently Kun Mountain burned and the seas churned; the realm became ruins and the people were charred.

sentences.zh: 布衣戎卒，鋤櫌棘矜，爭霸圖王，狐鳴蜂起。

translations.literal: Cloth-robed soldiers and common troops, hoes and spiked staves in hand, contended for hegemony and plotted kingship; foxes cried and hornets rose.
translations.idiomatic: Common soldiers with hoes and staves contended for empire; rebels rose like foxes crying and hornets swarming.

sentences.zh: 翼翼京洛，強弩圍城；

translations.literal: The stately capital of Jing and Luo—strong crossbows besieged the walls;
translations.idiomatic: The stately capitals were besieged by strong crossbows;

sentences.zh: 膴膴周原，僵屍滿路。

translations.literal: the broad plains of Zhou—stiff corpses filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: the broad Zhou plain—stiff corpses filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 主上南巡，泛膠舟而忘返；

translations.literal: The ruler toured south, floating on a glue boat and forgetting to return;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor toured south on his pleasure boat and forgot to return;

sentences.zh: 匈奴北熾，將被髮于伊川。

translations.literal: the Xiongnu blazed in the north, about to let their hair down on the Yi River.
translations.idiomatic: the Xiongnu pressed from the north, about to overrun the Yi River.

sentences.zh: 輦上無虞，群下結舌，大盜移國，莫之敢指。

translations.literal: Above the carriage there was no warning; below all bit their tongues—the great thief shifted the state and none dared point at him.
translations.idiomatic: The court saw no danger; officials bit their tongues—the great thief stole the state and none dared accuse him.

sentences.zh: 忽焉至此，自貽伊戚，七百之基，窮於二世。

translations.literal: Suddenly it came to this—he brought calamity on himself; a foundation of seven hundred years ended in the second generation.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly it came to this—he brought ruin on himself; a foundation of seven hundred years ended in the second generation.

sentences.zh: 周、齊以往，書契以還，邦國淪胥，未有如斯之酷者也。

translations.literal: From Zhou and Qi onward, since written contracts began—states have fallen together, but never cruelty like this.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhou and Qi, since records began—states have fallen, but never with cruelty like this.

sentences.zh: 天生蒸民，必有司牧，當今為牧，非子而誰？

translations.literal: Heaven born the people and there must be a shepherd—who but you should shepherd today?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven born the people and there must be a shepherd—who but you should rule today?

sentences.zh: 老夫年餘知命，願不及此，欣戴大弟，攀鱗附翼。

translations.literal: This old man is past fifty and does not aspire to that; I gladly support my great younger brother, clinging to dragon scales and attaching to wings.
translations.idiomatic: I am past fifty and do not aspire to rule; I gladly support my great younger brother, clinging to the dragon's scales.

sentences.zh: 惟冀早應圖籙，以寧兆庶。

translations.literal: I only hope you soon answer the charts and tallies to bring peace to the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: I only hope you soon answer Heaven's signs and bring peace to the millions.

sentences.zh: 宗盟之長，屬籍見容；

translations.literal: As chief of the clan alliance, let my lineage be received;
translations.idiomatic: As chief of the alliance, receive me among your kin;

sentences.zh: 復封于唐，斯榮足矣！

translations.literal: enfeoffed again in Tang—that glory is enough!
translations.idiomatic: enfeoffed again in Tang—that honor is enough!

sentences.zh: 殪商辛於牧野，所不忍言；

translations.literal: Slaying Shang Xin at Muye—what I cannot bear to speak of;
translations.idiomatic: Slaying the tyrant at Muye—what I cannot bear to speak of;

sentences.zh: 執子嬰於咸陽，非敢聞命。

translations.literal: seizing Ziying at Xianyang—I dare not hear such orders.
translations.idiomatic: seizing Ziying at Xianyang—I dare not accept such orders.

sentences.zh: 汾、晉左右，尚須安輯，盟津之會，未暇卜期，今日鑾輿南幸，恐同永嘉之勢。

translations.literal: Left and right of Fen and Jin still need settling; the meeting at Meng Ford has no date yet chosen—today the imperial carriage tours south, and I fear it will be like the Yongjia era.
translations.idiomatic: Fen and Jin still need settling; the meeting at Meng Ford cannot yet be scheduled—today the emperor tours south, and I fear a repeat of the Yongjia disaster.

sentences.zh: 顧此中原，鞠為茂草，興言感歎，實疚於懷。

translations.literal: Looking on this central plain, overgrown with rank grass, I speak and sigh—truly it pains my breast.
translations.idiomatic: Looking on the central plain overgrown with weeds, I sigh with real pain in my heart.

sentences.zh: 脫知動靜，數遲貽報，未面靈襟，用增勞軫。

translations.literal: If I learn your movements, reports have been delayed; we have not met face to face, which increases my toil and care.
translations.idiomatic: If I learn your movements, forgive delayed reports; not meeting face to face increases my cares.

sentences.zh: 名利之地，鋒鏑縱橫，深慎垂堂，勉茲鴻業。

translations.literal: The place of fame and profit—blades and spears cross everywhere; deeply beware the hall's edge and strive on this great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Fame and profit draw blades on every side—take great care and strive on with your great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 密得書甚悅，示其部下曰：「唐公見推，天下不足定也！

translations.literal: Mi received the letter and was greatly pleased; he showed his subordinates: "The Duke of Tang promotes me—the realm is not hard to settle!
translations.idiomatic: Mi was greatly pleased by the letter and told his followers, "The Duke of Tang promotes me—the realm is as good as settled!

sentences.zh: 」於是不虞義師而專意於世充。

translations.literal: " He therefore did not beware the righteous army and focused solely on Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore paid no heed to the Tang army and focused solely on Shichong.

sentences.zh: 俄而宇文化及率眾自江都北指黎陽，兵十餘萬，密乃自將步騎二萬拒之。

translations.literal: Soon Yuwen Huaji led his host north from Jiangdu toward Liyang with more than a hundred thousand troops; Mi personally led twenty thousand foot and horse to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuwen Huaji marched north from Jiangdu toward Liyang with more than a hundred thousand men; Mi personally led twenty thousand foot and horse to resist him.

sentences.zh: 隋越王侗稱尊號，遣使授密太尉、尚書令、東南道大行台行軍元帥、魏國公，令先平化及，然後入朝輔政。

translations.literal: The Sui Prince of Yue Yang Tong assumed the exalted title and sent envoys to invest Mi as Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Campaign Marshal of the Southeast Circuit Grand Commissioner, and Duke of Wei, ordering him first to pacify Huaji and then enter court to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tong, the Sui Prince of Yue, assumed the imperial title and invested Mi as Grand Commandant, Director of State Affairs, Southeast Campaign Marshal, and Duke of Wei, ordering him to pacify Huaji first and then enter court as regent.

sentences.zh: 密將與化及相抗，恐前後受敵，因卑辭以報謝焉。

translations.literal: Mi was about to resist Huaji and feared being attacked front and rear; he therefore used humble words in reply to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was about to fight Huaji and feared attack from both sides; he therefore replied with humble thanks.

sentences.zh: 化及至黎陽，與密相遇，密知其軍少食，利在急戰，故不與交鋒，又遏其歸路。

translations.literal: Huaji reached Liyang and met Mi; Mi knew his army had little food and that advantage lay in swift battle, so he did not cross blades and also blocked his route of return.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji reached Liyang and met Mi; Mi knew his army was short of food and that haste favored the enemy, so he refused battle and blocked Huaji's retreat.

sentences.zh: 密遣徐世勣守倉城，化及攻之不能下。

translations.literal: Mi sent Xu Shiji to guard the granary city; Huaji attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi sent Xu Shiji to guard the granary city; Huaji attacked but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 密知化及糧且盡，因偽與和，以弊其眾。

translations.literal: Mi knew Huaji's grain was nearly exhausted and therefore feigned peace to wear down his host.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Huaji's grain was nearly gone, Mi feigned peace to wear down his army.

sentences.zh: 化及弗之悟，大喜，恣其兵食，冀密饋之。

translations.literal: Huaji did not perceive the trick, was greatly pleased, and let his troops eat freely, hoping Mi would feed them.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji did not see through it, was delighted, and let his men eat freely, hoping Mi would supply them.

sentences.zh: 後知其計，化及怒，與密大戰于衛州之童山下，密為流矢所中，頓於汲縣。

translations.literal: Later learning the stratagem, Huaji was enraged and fought a great battle with Mi below Tong Mountain in Weizhou; Mi was struck by a stray arrow and halted at Ji County.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the trick, Huaji was enraged and fought Mi below Tong Mountain in Weizhou; Mi was wounded by a stray arrow and halted at Ji County.

sentences.zh: 化及力竭糧盡，眾多叛之，掠汲縣，北趣魏縣。

translations.literal: Huaji's strength was spent and grain exhausted; many rebelled against him; he plundered Ji County and headed north toward Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji's strength and grain were spent; many deserted him; he plundered Ji County and fled north toward Wei County.

sentences.zh: 其將陳智略、張童仁等率所部兵歸於密者，前後相繼。

translations.literal: His generals Chen Zhilue, Zhang Tongren, and others leading their troops to submit to Mi came one after another.
translations.idiomatic: His generals Chen Zhilue, Zhang Tongren, and others brought their troops over to Mi in succession.

sentences.zh: 初，化及留輜重於東郡，遣其所署刑部尚書王軌守之，至是軌舉郡降密。

translations.literal: Initially Huaji left baggage trains in Dong Commandery and sent his appointed Minister of Justice Wang Gui to guard it; at this time Gui surrendered the whole commandery to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji had left supplies in Dong Commandery under his Minister of Justice Wang Gui; Gui now surrendered the whole commandery to Mi.

sentences.zh: 密引兵而西，遣使朝於東都，執弑煬帝人于弘達獻越王侗。

translations.literal: Mi led his troops west and sent envoys to court at the Eastern Capital, seizing Yu Hongda, who had killed Emperor Yang, and presenting him to the Prince of Yue Yang Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Mi marched west and sent envoys to the Eastern Capital court, capturing Yu Hongda, who had killed Emperor Yang, and presenting him to Yang Tong.

sentences.zh: 侗召密入朝，至溫縣，聞世充作難而止，乃歸金墉城。

translations.literal: Tong summoned Mi to court; reaching Wen County he heard Shichong had raised trouble and stopped, then returned to Jinyong city.
translations.idiomatic: Tong summoned Mi to court; at Wen County he heard Shichong had rebelled and turned back to Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 時密兵少衣，世充兵乏食，乃請交易，密初難之，邴元真好求私利，屢勸密，密遂許焉。

translations.literal: At the time Mi's troops lacked clothing and Shichong's lacked food; they requested trade. Mi at first found it difficult; Bing Yuanzhen loved seeking private profit and repeatedly urged Mi, and Mi then agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's troops lacked clothing and Shichong's lacked food; they proposed trade. Mi hesitated, but Bing Yuanzhen, eager for private gain, urged him repeatedly, and Mi agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，東都絕糧，兵士歸密者日有數百，至此得食，而降人益少，密方悔而止。

translations.literal: Initially the Eastern Capital had no grain and soldiers submitting to Mi came by hundreds each day; now they got food and surrenders grew fewer—Mi then regretted it and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital had no grain, hundreds of soldiers defected to Mi daily; once they were fed at Mi's camp, defections slowed—Mi regretted the trade and tried to stop it.

sentences.zh: 密雖據倉而無府庫，兵數戰皆不獲賞，又厚撫初附之兵，由是眾心漸怨。

translations.literal: Though Mi held the granary he had no treasury; troops fought repeatedly without receiving rewards, and he also treated newly attached soldiers generously—therefore hearts gradually resented.
translations.idiomatic: Though Mi held the granaries he had no treasury; his troops fought repeatedly without reward, while he lavished gifts on new recruits—resentment spread.

sentences.zh: 九月，世充以其眾五千來決戰，密留王伯當守金墉，自引精兵就偃師，北阻邙山以待之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Shichong came with five thousand of his host for a decisive battle; Mi left Wang Bodang to guard Jinyong and personally led elite troops to Yanshi, blocking north at Mount Mang to await him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Shichong came with five thousand men for a decisive battle; Mi left Wang Bodang at Jinyong and led elite troops to Yanshi, blocking Mount Mang to the north.

sentences.zh: 世充軍至，密遂敗績，裴仁基、祖君彥並為世充所虜，密與萬餘人馳向洛口。

translations.literal: When Shichong's army arrived Mi was defeated; Pei Renji and Zu Junyan were both captured by Shichong; Mi with more than ten thousand men galloped toward Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong arrived Mi was defeated; Pei Renji and Zu Junyan were captured; Mi fled toward Luokou with more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 世充圍偃師，守將鄭頲之下兵士劫叛，以城降世充。

translations.literal: Shichong besieged Yanshi; under defender Zheng Ting the soldiers mutinied and surrendered the city to Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong besieged Yanshi; under defender Zheng Ting the garrison mutinied and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 密將入洛口倉城，邴元真已遣人潛引世充，密陰知之，不發其事，欲待世充兵半渡洛水，然後擊之。

translations.literal: Mi was about to enter the Luokou granary city; Bing Yuanzhen had already secretly sent men to bring in Shichong. Mi knew in secret but did not expose it, wishing to wait until Shichong's troops were half across the Luo River and then strike.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was about to enter Luokou granary city; Bing Yuanzhen had secretly invited Shichong in. Mi knew but kept silent, planning to strike when half of Shichong's army was across the Luo.

sentences.zh: 及世充軍至，密候騎不時覺，比將出戰，世充軍已濟矣。

translations.literal: When Shichong's army arrived Mi's scouts did not notice in time; by the time he was about to give battle Shichong's army had already crossed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong arrived Mi's scouts failed to warn him in time; before he could fight, Shichong's army had already crossed.

sentences.zh: 密自度不能支，引騎而遁，徑赴武牢，元真竟以城降於世充。

translations.literal: Mi judged he could not hold, led his cavalry in flight, and went straight to Wulao; Yuanzhen in the end surrendered the city to Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not hold, Mi fled with his cavalry straight to Wulao; Yuanzhen surrendered the city to Shichong.

sentences.zh: 密將如黎陽，或謂密曰：「殺翟讓之際，徐世勣幾至於死，今向其所，安可保乎？

translations.literal: Mi was about to go to Liyang; someone said to Mi: "When Zhai Rang was killed Xu Shiji nearly died—now going to his place, how can you be safe?
translations.idiomatic: Mi was about to go to Liyang when someone said, "When you killed Zhai Rang, Xu Shiji nearly died—how can you be safe going to him now?

sentences.zh: 」時王伯當棄金墉，保河陽，密以輕騎自武牢歸之，謂伯當曰：「兵敗矣，久苦諸君！

translations.literal: " At the time Wang Bodang had abandoned Jinyong and held Heyang; Mi with light cavalry came from Wulao to join him and said to Bodang: "We are defeated—I have long burdened you all!
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Bodang had abandoned Jinyong and held Heyang; Mi came from Wulao with light cavalry and told him, "We are defeated—I have long burdened you all!

sentences.zh: 我今自刎，請以謝眾。

translations.literal: I will now cut my own throat to answer to the host.
translations.idiomatic: I will now take my own life to answer to the army.

sentences.zh: 」伯當抱密，號叫慟絕，眾皆泣，莫能仰視。

translations.literal: " Bodang embraced Mi, wailing until grief cut off his breath; all wept and none could look up.
translations.idiomatic: " Bodang embraced him and wailed until he could breathe no more; all wept and none could bear to look.

sentences.zh: 密復曰：「諸軍幸不相棄，當共歸關中，密身雖愧無功，諸君必保富貴。

translations.literal: Mi again said: "You armies, I hope you will not abandon me—we should return together to Guanzhong. Though I am ashamed to be without merit, you will surely keep wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said again, "If you will not abandon me, let us return together to Guanzhong. Though I have achieved nothing, you will surely keep wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 」其府掾柳奭對曰：「昔盆子歸漢，尚食均輸。

translations.literal: " His bureau aide Liu Shuang replied: "Formerly Penzi submitted to Han and was made Director of Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: " His aide Liu Shuang replied, "When Penzi submitted to Han he was made Director of Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 明公與唐公同族，兼有疇昔之遇，雖不陪從起義，然而阻東都，斷隋歸路，使唐公不戰而據京師，此亦公之功也。

translations.literal: My lord and the Duke of Tang are of the same clan and also share an old acquaintance; though you did not accompany the uprising, you blocked the Eastern Capital and cut the Sui return route, letting the Duke of Tang take the capital without battle—this too is my lord's merit.
translations.idiomatic: You and the Duke of Tang are kin and have old ties; though you did not join the uprising, you blocked the Eastern Capital and cut the Sui line of retreat, letting the Tang take the capital without a fight—that is your merit too.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸曰：「然。

translations.literal: " All said: "It is so.
translations.idiomatic: " All agreed.

sentences.zh: 」密又謂王伯當曰：「將軍室家重大，豈復與孤俱行哉！

translations.literal: " Mi also said to Wang Bodang: "General, your household is weighty—how could you again travel with me alone!
translations.idiomatic: " Mi also told Wang Bodang, "General, your family is a heavy burden—you need not travel with me!

sentences.zh: 」伯當曰：「昔漢高誅項，蕭何率子弟以從，伯當恨不昆季盡從，以此為愧耳。

translations.literal: " Bodang said: "Formerly when Han Gaozu executed Xiang Yu, Xiao He led his sons and younger brothers to follow—I regret that not all my brothers followed; that is my shame.
translations.idiomatic: " Bodang said, "When Han Gaozu destroyed Xiang Yu, Xiao He brought his brothers and sons to follow—I regret that not all my brothers came; that is my shame.

sentences.zh: 豈以公今日失利，遂輕去就？

translations.literal: How could I lightly leave because my lord fails today?
translations.idiomatic: How could I abandon you because you fail today?

sentences.zh: 縱身分原野，亦所甘心。

translations.literal: Even if my body lies in the wilds, I am content.
translations.idiomatic: Even if I die in the wilds, I am content.

sentences.zh: 」左右莫不感激，於是從入關者尚二萬人。

translations.literal: " Those left and right were all moved; those who followed into the passes still numbered twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: " All were deeply moved; twenty thousand still followed him into the passes.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣使迎勞，相望於道，密大喜，謂其徒曰：「我有眾百萬，一朝至此，命也。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor sent envoys to welcome and comfort him, one meeting another on the road; Mi was greatly pleased and told his followers: "I had a host of a million and in one morning came to this—it is fate.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor sent envoys to welcome him along the road; Mi was overjoyed and told his followers, "I once commanded a million men and in a morning came to this—it is fate.

sentences.zh: 今事敗歸國，幸蒙殊遇，當思竭忠以事所奉耳！

translations.literal: Now defeated I return to the state and am fortunate to receive special treatment—I should think to exhaust loyalty in serving whom I follow!
translations.idiomatic: Now defeated I return and am treated with special favor—I must serve my new lord with all loyalty!

sentences.zh: 且山東連城數百，知吾至此，遣使招之，盡當歸國。

translations.literal: Moreover the linked cities of Shandong number in the hundreds—knowing I have come here, if I send envoys to summon them, all will return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover hundreds of cities in Shandong will send envoys when they learn I am here, and all will return to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 比于竇融，勳亦不細，豈不以一臺司見處乎？

translations.literal: Compared with Dou Rong, his merit is not slight—should he not be treated with the regard due a commissioner?
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Dou Rong, his merit was considerable—was he not worthy of a commissioner's regard?

sentences.zh: 」及至京師，禮數益薄，執政者又來求賄，意甚不平。

translations.literal: " When he reached the capital, ceremonial courtesies grew ever thinner; those in power again came seeking bribes—his mind was very resentful.
translations.idiomatic: " In the capital, ceremonial courtesies grew thin, and those in power came seeking bribes—he grew deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 尋拜光祿卿，封邢國公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，聞其所部將帥皆不附世充，高祖使密領本兵往黎陽，招集故時將士，經略世充。

translations.literal: Before long, hearing that the generals and commanders of his former following would not attach to Shichong, the High Ancestor had Mi lead his original troops to Liyang to gather his former officers and plan against Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon hearing that his former generals would not follow Shichong, the High Ancestor sent Mi with his original troops to Liyang to rally his old officers and operate against Shichong.

sentences.zh: 時王伯當為左武衛將軍，亦令為副。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Bodang was General of the Left Martial Guard and was also ordered as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bodang was then General of the Left Martial Guard and was appointed his deputy.

sentences.zh: 密行至桃林，高祖復徵之，密大懼，謀將叛。

translations.literal: Mi traveled to Taolin; the High Ancestor summoned him again—Mi was greatly afraid and plotted to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi reached Taolin, the High Ancestor summoned him again; terrified, Mi plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 伯當頗止之，密不從，因謂密曰：「義士之立志也，不以存亡易心。

translations.literal: Bodang strongly tried to stop him; Mi would not listen and therefore said to Mi: "A man of honor in setting his will does not change his heart for survival or destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Bodang urged him strongly to stop, but Mi refused and told him, "A man of honor does not change his heart whether he lives or dies.

sentences.zh: 伯當荷公恩禮，期以性命相報。

translations.literal: Bodang bears my lord's grace and courtesy and expects to repay you with my life.
translations.idiomatic: I have received your grace and expect to repay you with my life.

sentences.zh: 公必不聽，今祗可同去，死生以之，然終恐無益也。

translations.literal: My lord surely will not listen—now I can only go with you, for life or death, yet in the end I fear it will be of no use.
translations.idiomatic: If you will not listen, I can only go with you, for life or death—though I fear it will come to nothing.

sentences.zh: 」乃簡驍勇數千人，著婦人衣，戴幕離，藏刀裙下，詐為妻妾，自率之入桃林縣舍。

translations.literal: " He then selected several thousand fierce brave men, dressed them in women's clothes, put on veiled hats, hid knives beneath their skirts, pretended to be wives and concubines, and personally led them into the Taolin county quarters.
translations.idiomatic: " He selected several thousand fierce men, dressed them as women with veiled hats and knives hidden under their skirts, posed them as wives and concubines, and led them into the Taolin county quarters.

sentences.zh: 須臾，變服突出，因據縣城，驅掠畜產，直趣南山，乘險而東，遣人馳告張善相，令以兵應接。

translations.literal: In a moment they changed clothes and burst forth, seized the county city, drove off livestock, headed straight for South Mountain, took the defiles eastward, and sent men galloping to inform Zhang Shanxiang to bring troops to link up.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment they changed clothes and burst out, seized the county seat, drove off livestock, headed for South Mountain, took the defiles east, and sent word to Zhang Shanxiang to bring troops to meet them.

sentences.zh: 時右翊衛將軍史萬寶留鎮熊州，遣副將盛彥師率步騎數千追躡，至陸渾縣南七十里，與密相及。

translations.literal: At the time the Right Assistant Guard General Shi Wanbao was left to garrison Xiongzhou; he sent Vice-General Sheng Yanshi with several thousand foot and horse in pursuit. Seventy li south of Luhun County he caught Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Right Assistant Guard General Shi Wanbao was garrisoning Xiongzhou; he sent Vice-General Sheng Yanshi with several thousand foot and horse in pursuit, and caught Mi seventy li south of Luhun County.

sentences.zh: 彥師伏兵山谷，密軍半度，橫出擊，敗之，遂斬密，時年三十七。

translations.literal: Yanshi hid troops in the valley; when Mi's army was half across he struck out horizontally, defeated them, and beheaded Mi—he was thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi ambushed him in the valley; when Mi's force was half across, he struck, routed them, and beheaded Mi, aged thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 王伯當亦死之，與密俱傳首京師。

translations.literal: Wang Bodang also died for it; with Mi their heads were sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bodang died with him; their heads were sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時李勣為黎陽總管，高祖以勣舊經事密，遣使報其反狀。

translations.literal: At the time Li Ji was Director-General of Liyang; the High Ancestor, because Ji had formerly served Mi, sent envoys to report his rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji was then Director-General of Liyang; because he had once served Mi, the High Ancestor sent word of Mi's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 勣表請收葬，詔許之。

translations.literal: Ji memorialized requesting to gather and bury him; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji petitioned to bury him properly, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 高祖歸其屍，勣發喪行服，備君臣之禮。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor returned his corpse; Ji held the funeral and wore mourning, providing the full rites of ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor returned his body; Ji held the funeral in mourning with full rites between lord and minister.

sentences.zh: 大具威儀，三軍皆縞素，葬于黎陽山南五里。

translations.literal: He fully arrayed ceremonial majesty; the three armies all wore white hemp, and burial was five li south of Liyang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony was conducted with full honors; the entire army wore mourning white, and he was buried five li south of Liyang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 故人哭之，多有歐血者。

translations.literal: Old friends wept for him; many vomited blood in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Old friends wept for him; many vomited blood from grief.

sentences.zh: 邴元真之降世充也，以為行臺僕射，鎮滑州。

translations.literal: When Bing Yuanzhen surrendered to Shichong he was made Grand Commissioner Vice Director and garrisoned Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Bing Yuanzhen surrendered to Shichong, he was made Grand Commissioner Vice Director and posted to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 密故將杜才幹恨元真背密，詐與之會，伏甲斬之，以其首祭於密塚。

translations.literal: Mi's former general Du Caigan hated Yuanzhen for betraying Mi; he feigned a meeting with him, hid armored men, and cut him down, offering his head in sacrifice at Mi's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's former general Du Caigan hated Yuanzhen for betraying Mi; he lured him to a meeting, ambushed and killed him, and offered his head at Mi's tomb.

sentences.zh: 單雄信單雄信者，曹州人也。

translations.literal: Shan Xiongxin—Shan Xiongxin was a man of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Xiongxin was from Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 翟讓與之友善。

translations.literal: Zhai Rang was friendly with him.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with Zhai Rang.

sentences.zh: 少驍健，尤能馬上用槍，密軍號為「飛將」。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and strong, especially able with the spear on horseback; Mi's army called him the "Flying General."
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was fierce and strong, especially skilled with the spear on horseback; Mi's army called him the Flying General.

sentences.zh: 密偃師失利，遂降于王世充，署為大將軍。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated at Yanshi he surrendered to Wang Shichong and was appointed Great General.
translations.idiomatic: After Mi's defeat at Yanshi, he surrendered to Wang Shichong and was made Great General.

sentences.zh: 太宗圍逼東都，雄信出軍拒戰，援槍而至，幾及太宗，徐世勣呵止之，曰：「此秦王也。

translations.literal: When the Taizong besieged the Eastern Capital, Xiongxin led troops out to resist; spear in hand he came up and nearly reached the Taizong—Xu Shiji shouted to stop him, saying: "This is the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong besieged the Eastern Capital, Xiongxin came out to fight; spear in hand he nearly reached Taizong when Xu Shiji shouted to stop him, saying, "This is the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 」雄信惶懼，遂退，太宗由是獲免。

translations.literal: " Xiongxin was fearful and withdrew; the Taizong thereby escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiongxin withdrew in fear, and Taizong was spared.

sentences.zh: 東都平，斬於洛陽。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified he was executed at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital fell, he was executed at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：當隋政板蕩，煬帝荒淫，搖動中原，遠征遼海。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The historiographer says: When Sui government was in turmoil, Emperor Yang was dissolute and wanton, shaking the central plain and campaigning far to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: When Sui rule collapsed, Emperor Yang indulged in dissipation, shook the central plain, and campaigned far to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 內無賢臣以匡國，外乏良吏以理民，兩京空虛，兆庶疲弊。

translations.literal: Within there were no worthy ministers to correct the state; without there were no good officials to govern the people—the two capitals stood empty and the hundred millions were worn and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Within there were no worthy ministers to correct the state; without, no good officials to govern the people—the two capitals stood empty and the people were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 李密因民不忍，首為亂階，心斷機謀，身臨陣敵，據鞏、洛之口，號百萬之師，竇建德輩皆效樂推，唐公紿以欣戴，不亦偉哉！

translations.literal: Li Mi, because the people could not bear it, was first to make the ladder of disorder—his mind decisive in stratagem, his person facing battle in the ranks, holding the mouth of Gong and Luo, proclaiming an army of a million—Dou Jiande and his kind all imitated joyous elevation, and the Duke of Tang deceived him with delighted support—is it not grand!
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi, because the people could not endure it, was first to raise rebellion—clever in stratagem, brave in battle, holding the Gong and Luo corridor, proclaiming a million men—Dou Jiande and others rallied to him, and the Duke of Tang flattered him with feigned support—was it not magnificent!

sentences.zh: 及偃師失律，猶存麾下數萬眾，苟去猜忌，疾趣黎陽，任世勣為將臣，信魏徵為謀主，成敗之勢，或未可知。

translations.literal: When Yanshi was lost against plan he still had tens of thousands under his banner; if he had cast off suspicion, hastened to Liyang, entrusted Xu Shiji as general and minister, and trusted Wei Zheng as chief strategist—the trend of success or failure might still have been unknown.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat at Yanshi he still had tens of thousands; had he cast off suspicion, hurried to Liyang, made Xu Shiji his general and Wei Zheng his strategist, the outcome might still have been uncertain.

sentences.zh: 至於天命有歸，大事已去，比陳涉有餘矣。

translations.literal: As for Heaven's mandate having found its lord and the great affair already gone—compared with Chen She he had surplus.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven's mandate had found its lord and the great cause was lost, he still surpassed Chen She.

sentences.zh: 始則稱首舉兵，終乃甘心為降虜，其為計也，不亦危乎！

translations.literal: At first he was called the first to raise arms; in the end he was content to be a surrendered captive—his planning, was it not perilous!
translations.idiomatic: He began as the first to raise arms and ended willing to be a surrendered captive—his calculations were perilous indeed!

sentences.zh: 又不能委質為臣，竭誠事上，竟為叛者，終是狂夫，不取伯當之言，遂及桃林之禍。

translations.literal: He could not moreover surrender his substance as minister and exhaust loyalty in serving his superior—he ended a rebel, ultimately a madman; not taking Bodang's words, he thus met the disaster at Taolin.
translations.idiomatic: He could not submit as a loyal minister and serve with full devotion—he became a rebel, a madman in the end; ignoring Bodang's counsel, he met disaster at Taolin.

sentences.zh: 或以項羽擬之，文武器度即有餘，壯勇斷果則不及。

translations.literal: Some compare him to Xiang Yu—in literary accomplishment and weaponry he had surplus; in fierce courage and resolute decisiveness he did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Some compare him to Xiang Yu—in culture and bearing he had the advantage; in raw courage and decisive force he fell short.

sentences.zh: 楊素既知密之才幹，合為王之爪牙，委之癡兒，卒為謀主，覆族之禍，其宜也哉！

translations.literal: Yang Su already knew Mi's talent and capacity—he should have been the king's claw and fang; entrusted to a foolish son, he ended chief strategist—the calamity that overturned the clan: was it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su knew Mi's talent and should have made him the prince's right hand; instead he left him to a foolish son, and Mi became a rebel chief—the ruin of the clan was only to be expected!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：烏陽既升，爝火不息。

translations.literal: In praise it is said: When the dark sun has risen, torch fire does not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: When the dark sun rises, torch fires never cease.

sentences.zh: 狂哉李密，始亂終逆。

translations.literal: Mad was Li Mi—rebellion at the start, treason at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Mad was Li Mi—rebellion at the start, treason at the end.
